articles.abstract: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has emerged as a potential therapeutic strategy for cancer. However, intrinsic resistance, off-target toxicity, and poor redox efficiency limit the effectiveness of existing ferroptosis-inducing platforms. This study reports novel heparin-derived metal coordination nanoparticles (HDMC NP) that leverage catechol-metal-drug coordination chemistry to enhance ferroptosis and immunogenic cell death (ICD). In this self-assembled supramolecular system, doxorubicin (DOX) directly coordinates to Fe3+ centers established by catechol-Fe3+ interactions on the heparin backbone, forming a stable HDMC NP with high drug-loading efficiency. This coordination not only stabilizes the complex under neutral conditions but also triggers disassembly in response to pH changes in the tumor microenvironment. Notably, the DOX-Fe3+ pairing supports sustained redox activity, amplifying ROS production and ferroptotic stress in a coordination-dependent manner beyond the effect of either component alone. In animal models, HDMC NP suppresses tumor growth by inducing both ferroptosis and ICD, characterized by calreticulin exposure and CD8+ T cell infiltration. Collectively, this platform provides a redox-active nanotherapeutic based on coordination-defined assembly with potential for broad applications in metal-ion modulated diseases.

articles.title: Discovery of a small molecule RIOK1 inhibitor CINS-1 against colorectal cancer via disrupting ribosomal biosynthesis.
articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the most prevalent malignancies globally. Despite significant advancements in targeted therapies, drug resistance and therapeutic target mutations continue to pose challenges. Consequently, identifying novel therapeutic targets and developing related compounds are essential for discovering new CRC treatment strategies. The RIO Kinase 1 (RIOK1) protein has emerged as a potential anti-tumor target, playing a critical role in eukaryotic ribosomal biosynthesis and modulating cellular proliferation. However, few compounds have been designed to target RIOK1, and the antitumor activity of RIOK1 inhibitors has yet to be thoroughly investigated. In this study, we report the optimization of pyridine caffeic acid benzyl amide derivatives as RIOK1 inhibitors and identified CINS-1 as a potent compound with markedly enhanced binding affinity for AfRIOK1 and RIOK1. Notably, we elucidated the crystal structure of AfRIOK1 in complex with CINS-1. Our findings further confirm the inhibitory effects of CINS-1 on CRC cell proliferation both in vitro and in vivo. Additionally, CINS-1 was shown to disrupt ribosomal biosynthesis by hindering 18S maturation and triggering a P53-mediated nucleolar stress response. Overall, these results provide a theoretical and empirical basis for considering the RIOK1 inhibitor CINS-1 as a promising candidate for anti-CRC therapy.

articles.title: A mechanistic quantitative systems pharmacology framework enriched by multiscale data enables model-informed translational development of mesenchymal stem cell therapy in lupus nephritis.
articles.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is a complex autoimmune disease and mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), given their unique immune-modulatory potential, have emerged as a promising route for treating LN. Understanding the multiscale dynamic LN-MSC interactions and selecting the optimal clinical design for MSCs is critical to enhance their therapeutic potential and achieve meaningful benefit-risk differentiation in patients. To guide MSC clinical development, we constructed the first mechanistic quantitative systems pharmacology model of LN pathophysiology that integrated multimodal preclinical-clinical data, with detailed illustration of standard-of-care immunosuppressant pharmacology and physiologically-based biodistribution and therapeutic mechanisms of MSCs. We created model-based virtual LN patients that well captured clinical interpatient heterogeneity and were validated by numerous sets of clinical efficacy readouts, including first-hand results from our investigator-initiated trial testing MSCs in LN patients. We used this computational framework and identified that a spaced two-infusion MSC dosing strategy would yield optimal clinical response in LN patients, which directly informed the phase 2 design of a novel MSC therapy. Modeling analyses further identified that CXCL10 in combination with proteinuria are potential predictive biomarkers that could boost clinical renal response to MSCs. These results demonstrated the exceptional importance of our QSP framework in driving MSC clinical development for LN patients.

articles.title: Identification of FDA-approved IMPDH inhibitors boosting the broad-spectrum antiviral potential of ribavirin through depleting cellular GTP pool.
articles.abstract: Nucleoside analogues are among the most promising broad-spectrum antiviral agents. We developed a high-throughput synergistic screening system to identify US Food and Drug Administration-approved drugs that enhance the effectiveness of nucleoside analogues. Unlike conventional combination approaches, this strategy does not require boost agents to have direct antiviral activity; instead, they can enhance antiviral agent's effect through novel synergistic mechanisms. We identified mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), which significantly boosts ribavirin's (RBV) antiviral efficacy against influenza A virus, even at concentrations where MMF alone shows minimal activity. MMF enhances RBV by inhibiting IMPDH (inosine-5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase) and reducing cellular GTP levels, potentially increasing RBV incorporation and its antiviral potency. This mechanism was confirmed by adding exogenous GTP, which reversed the synergy. In a mouse model, MMF also enhanced RBV's effectiveness against PR8 in vivo. Moreover, MMF showed synergistic effects against other influenza subtypes and RNA viruses including ZIKV and HCoV-OC43, demonstrating the potential wide applicability of this strategy. Our study introduces a new screening system and identifies novel RBV combinations, offering a promising approach for developing effective broad-spectrum antiviral combinations against emerging viral threats.

articles.title: Ultra-sensitive detection of receptor binding domain of SARS-CoV-2 based on artificial intelligence assisted antibody selection and antibody‒nucleic acid conjugation signal amplification.
articles.abstract: The emergence of SARS-CoV-2 has led to a global pandemic, causing unprecedented disruption to health systems and economies worldwide, calling for an urgent imperative for precise and sensitive diagnostic method. To address this, a novel detection method, termed antibody‒nucleic acid conjugate linked immunosorbent assay (ANCLISA), was designed for the ultra-sensitive detection of the receptor binding domain (RBD) of SARS-CoV-2, which play a pivotal role in the diagnosis of COVID-19. Leveraging the Alphafold 2 model for simulating antibody‒antigen complexes and the ΔΔG predictor model for forecasting the binding free energy of antigen‒antibody complex, we successfully identified the high-affinity antibody TB1. Through the utilization of succinimidyl 4-[N-maleimidomethyl] cyclohexane-1-carboxylate (SMCC) for antibody‒nucleic acid conjugation and the integration of the hybridization chain reaction (HCR) for signal amplification within the system, we have established an ultra-sensitive approach for the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant detection. The proposed immunoassay provided exhibited a linear detection range spanning 11 fg/mL to 11 ng/mL, achieving a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.48 fg/mL. Our innovative approach represents a significant stride in enabling precise and ultra-sensitive detection of SARS-CoV-2, thereby holding promise for enhancing diagnostic capabilities in the ongoing global battle against the pandemic.

articles.title: Biosimilar Development Considerations for Therapeutic Proteins With Limited Systemic Exposure: A Landscape Analysis and Pathway Evaluation.
articles.abstract: Biosimilar development for therapeutic proteins (TPs) with limited systemic exposure presents distinct challenges, as the new paradigm based on comparative analytical assessments plus pharmacokinetic similarity without a comparative efficacy study (CES) is inapplicable. Of 19 TPs with limited systemic exposure, 15 are well-characterized, of which 12 have at least one CES-feasible indication. The remaining 3 may require alternative strategies, including pharmacodynamic (PD) biomarker approaches or optimized CES designs, underscoring the need for proactive regulatory engagement.

articles.title: Safety, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of ICP-332, an oral TYK2 inhibitor, in healthy participants: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase I study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: ICP-332 is a novel, orally administered TYK2 inhibitor with high selectivity, intended for the treatment of immune inflammatory diseases such as atopic dermatitis, psoriatic arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease and lupus. This Phase I study assessed its safety, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and food effect in Chinese healthy participants. METHODS: This study was designed as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in healthy participants. It consisted of a single-ascending-dose (SAD) part with six cohorts (5, 15, 40, 80, 160, and 320 mg) and a multiple-ascending-dose (MAD) part with three cohorts (40, 80, and 160 mg administered once daily for 14 days). Food-effect evaluation was included at the 80 mg SAD level. In each cohort, eight participants were randomized (6:2) to receive either ICP-332 or placebo. Following oral administration, plasma samples were collected to determine ICP-332 concentrations, and safety tolerance was monitored and assessed throughout the study. RESULTS: This study enrolled 72 healthy participants, with 48 and 24 completing the SAD and MAD phases, respectively. After oral administration, ICP-332 showed rapid absorption, with median time to peak concentration (T max) of 0.5-2.0 h and mean elimination half-life (t ½ ) of 2.692-7.275 h. Dose-proportional exposure was confirmed in both the SAD (5-320 mg) and MAD (40-160 mg) phases; area under the concentration-time curve (AUC last ) ranged from 146.3 to 11,667.5 h·ng/mL in the SAD phase and from 1386.0 to 6513.5 h·ng/mL at steady state in the MAD phase. ICP-332 also induced rapid and dose-dependent suppression of TYK2 activity, as evidenced by dose-related reductions in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein and a trend toward decreased interferon gamma-induced protein 10 levels versus placebo. In terms of safety, treatment-emergent adverse events were all mild to moderate in severity, with no participant withdrawals. TEAE incidence was comparable to placebo in the SAD phase and slightly higher in the MAD phase. CONCLUSION: ICP-332 exhibited favorable safety, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics profiles across the 5-320 mg dose range, with rapid absorption, dose-proportional exposure, and mild, reversible adverse events. A high-fat meal did not significantly affect its pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics or safety. These results support continued clinical development of ICP-332 as a promising treatment for autoimmune diseases. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: http://www.chinadrugtrials.org.cn/index.html CTR20211781.

articles.title: Illuminating the black box: Mapping the fates of polymeric micelle drug carriers in vivo.
miniPROTACs: Bridging PROTACs and molecular glues with a new degron alphabet.
Interpreting antiretroviral exposure and drug-drug interactions in pregnancy: A clinically anchored framework for HIV pharmacology.
articles.abstract: In pregnancy, antiretroviral drug-drug interactions must be interpreted against dynamic changes in gastrointestinal physiology, plasma-protein binding, renal elimination, hepatic enzyme activity and membrane transporter expression. Interaction studies quantify geometric mean exposure ratios relative to nonpregnant adults, but these measures describe relative pharmacokinetic change rather than whether effective exposure is preserved. For HIV treatment, validated exposure-response targets remain reasonable starting anchors when pregnancy-specific targets are unavailable. No evidence indicates that gestational immune adaptation alone requires a different intrinsic antiviral target. Pregnancy alters target attainment by altering drug disposition and variability, and it can modify the pharmacokinetics of both the victim antiretroviral and the perpetrator drug. For long-acting injectable PrEP, protective exposure, dosing interval and pharmacokinetic tail require separate consideration from treatment targets. This review evaluates candidate evidentiary anchors, including protein-adjusted in vitro inhibitory concentrations, exposure-response relationships, therapeutic drug-monitoring targets and model-informed probability of target attainment. Evidence from integrase inhibitors, protease inhibitors, non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, tenofovir formulations and long-acting agents demonstrates that similar proportional reductions in exposure can have different clinical implications depending on therapeutic margin, resistance barrier, interaction mechanism, formulation and pharmacologically relevant matrix. A newly proposed six-domain framework integrates clinical context, active analyte, exposure metric, evidentiary anchor, distributional target attainment and clinical outcomes. Physiologically based and population pharmacokinetic models provide evidence when pregnancy-specific data are unavailable, but their use should reflect model verification and uncertainty. The central objective is therefore not to define a universal pregnancy threshold but to determine whether pharmacologically effective exposure is maintained in the setting of gestational physiology and concomitant medicines.

articles.title: Letter to Editor: Clarifying the classification of normal organ biodistribution in a meta-analysis of polymeric Micelle Tumour delivery.
Glycine as a context-dependent excipient in protein-based biopharmaceutical formulations.
articles.abstract: Glycine is widely used as an excipient in protein-based biopharmaceutical formulations, yet its functions are often described too broadly, particularly in terms of stabilization. This review critically examines the physicochemical basis and formulation behavior of glycine across liquid, frozen, and freeze-dried systems, with emphasis on how its effects are governed by formulation composition, physical state, and processing history. Available evidence shows that glycine can contribute to several formulation functions, but its performance is highly product- and condition-dependent. In particular, crystallization represents a central feature of glycine-containing systems because it can support physical robustness and process performance while also creating risks associated with phase separation and loss of local stabilization. This benefit-risk balance depends on the extent of crystallization, the composition of the residual amorphous phase, and the surrounding formulation environment. These outcomes are further modified by interactions with sugars, buffers, surfactants, salts, and other excipients. Evidence from marketed protein-based biopharmaceutical products is also considered to place these mechanistic observations in a practical context. The review also identifies important evidence gaps, particularly in high-concentration protein formulations and in understanding how glycine physical state interacts with other formulation components. Overall, glycine is a multifunctional, physical-state- and process-dependent excipient, and its use should be supported by direct characterization of physical state and product-specific stability.

articles.title: Maternal-placental-fetal physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling: current approaches and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Fetal drug exposure is governed by maternal, placental, and fetal pharmacokinetic processes, among which placental drug transfer plays a central role. However, clinical data in pregnant populations remain limited, creating uncertainty in balancing maternal treatment needs with potential fetal risk. AREAS COVERED: Maternal-placental-fetal physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models provide a mechanistic framework to predict maternal and fetal exposure. This review summarizes the key placental physiological determinants of drug transfer and outlines the current landscape of maternal-placental-fetal PBPK models, including model structures, parameterization strategies, and applications in fetal exposure prediction and exposure-based risk assessment. Strengths and limitations of different data sources were also reviewed, including in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo data. A PubMed literature search was conducted, with the final search completed on 10 September 2026, to identify relevant maternal-placental-fetal PBPK studies. EXPERT OPINION: Based on perspectives from clinical obstetrics and PBPK modeling, we highlight the need for standardized modeling practices, improved integration of experimental data, transparent characterization of uncertainty, and clinically interpretable model outputs to support medication decision-making during pregnancy. Our goal is to support individualized risk-benefit assessment during pregnancy and inform both clinical practice and regulatory decision-making.

articles.title: Learn from nature, surpass nature: Bionic immune cell engineering-A new paradigm for unlocking the dual "delivery-activation" code in cancer therapy.
PANoptosis: a novel therapeutic target and mechanistic insight into traditional Chinese medicine intervention in inflammatory bowel disease: a review.
articles.abstract: The rising incidence of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and the limited efficacy of current therapies underscore the need for novel strategies. PANoptosis is an inflammatory programmed cell-death process integrating molecular features of pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis. Emerging evidence suggests that PANoptosis-related genes and signaling nodes may contribute to intestinal epithelial injury, mucosal immune activation, barrier disruption, and inflammatory amplification in inflammatory bowel disease. Traditional Chinese medicine and its active constituents have been reported to regulate inflammation, intestinal barrier integrity, gut microbiota, and several cell-death pathways. However, direct evidence that these agents inhibit bona fide PANoptosis in intestinal models remains limited. Current mechanistic evidence is strongest for selected compounds, such as baicalin, which has been shown in macrophages to interfere with mitochondrial Z-DNA formation and ZBP1-PANoptosome assembly, whereas other proposed mechanisms are largely extrapolated from extra-intestinal models or from studies of apoptosis, pyroptosis, necroptosis, and inflammatory signaling. This narrative review summarizes the molecular basis of PANoptosis in IBD and critically evaluates the potential of traditional Chinese medicine-derived compounds and formulas to modulate upstream sensors, adaptor proteins, and downstream effectors of PANoptosis-related pathways. We emphasize that future studies should verify these mechanisms in intestinal epithelial cells, intestinal organoids, DSS/TNBS/IL-10-deficient colitis models, and human IBD tissues.

articles.title: Mechanisms of traditional Chinese medicine interventions in the gastric 'inflammation-to-carcinoma' cascade: advances in in vitro models from monolayer cells to organoids.
articles.abstract: Gastric cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The Correa cascade, progressing from chronic gastritis through precancerous lesions to adenocarcinoma, provides the framework for understanding gastric mucosal stepwise malignant transformation. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulas, such as Zuojin Pills and Wuji Pills, have been historically used to treat gastric disorders including epigastric pain and acid regurgitation, yet their mechanisms of action in blocking the inflammation-to-carcinoma transition remain incompletely understood. The mechanistic diversity of TCM presents challenges for in vitro modeling, and existing reviews have not systematically addressed how model selection should align with specific research questions across different stages of the cascade. This review examines the evolving landscape of in vitro models used in TCM research on gastric mucosal inflammation-to-carcinoma transition, highlighting the paradigm shift from two-dimensional (2D) monolayer GES-1 cell cultures to three-dimensional gastric organoids. We analyzed recent studies conducted across multiple model platforms using various acute or chronic pathogenic factors, with all botanical drugs validated taxonomically through authoritative sources. The GES-1 cell model offers low cost, high throughput, and genetic homogeneity, making it suitable for initial screening of active metabolites from botanical drugs and for dissecting molecular pathways, particularly those involving Nrf2, NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, and MAPK signaling in antioxidative stress, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic mechanisms. In contrast, gastric organoids preserve three-dimensional architecture, cellular diversity, and patient-specific genetic backgrounds, enabling functional assessment of barrier integrity, stem cell-driven regeneration, and malignant transformation at the tissue level. To address the need for evidence differentiation, we introduce a hierarchical framework (Model Evidence Level) in which GES-1 cells serve for entry-level target discovery and patient-derived organoids for higher-level tissue validation. Based on this framework, we provide stage-specific model selection recommendations corresponding to the distinct phases of the Correa cascade: acute inflammation, chronic atrophy, intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, and gastric cancer. This review offers a practical, evidence-stratified pathway for in vitro model selection in TCM intervention studies, bridging traditional ethnopharmacological knowledge with modern pharmacological validation to strengthen the translational relevance of preclinical findings.

articles.title: Plant-derived nanovesicles in kidney disease: emerging preclinical evidence and translational challenges.
articles.abstract: Plant-derived nanovesicles (PDNVs) are lipid-bilayer nanoparticles isolated from plant extracellular fluids, juices, or tissues. Preparations obtained from disrupted tissues may contain both extracellular vesicles and membrane particles formed during processing, making product identity central to interpretation. Seven direct renal studies have examined native or engineered PDNVs in cisplatin- and sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, diabetic kidney disease, hyperuricemia-associated renal injury, and calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis. Current evidence supports three overlapping modes of use: renal cellular protection, oral modulation of intestinal and metabolic pathways, and engineered cargo delivery. Reported effects involve mitochondrial function, endoplasmic reticulum stress, ferroptosis, inflammation, microbiota, and host metabolism, but mechanistic support is uneven. SLC7A11 perturbation provides functional evidence for ferroptosis in one model, whereas most microbiota-metabolite-kidney relationships remain associative. Fluorescent tissue signals also do not establish intact-vesicle delivery or cell-specific kidney targeting. This review distinguishes direct renal PDNV evidence from adjacent plant-bioactive nanomedicines and phytochemical-modified mammalian extracellular vesicles, and critically examines product identity, preparation, dose, biodistribution, mechanism, safety, and clinical translation. No registered renal PDNV trial was identified; existing human studies concern nonrenal mucosal or intestinal applications and plant-vesicle-assisted cargo delivery. Progress toward renal translation will depend on reproducible manufacturing, mechanism-linked potency, quantitative biodistribution, causal validation, and repeated-dose safety.

articles.title: Phenotype-informed selection of microbiota-directed interventions in irritable bowel syndrome: current evidence and limitations.
articles.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a heterogeneous disorder of gut-brain interaction in which bowel-habit subtype, dominant symptoms, post-infectious onset, bile-acid handling, visceral sensitivity, and diet-microbiota interactions may influence the treatment response. This narrative mini-review asks whether available clinical evidence is sufficient to select or sequence microbiota-directed and microbiota-modulating interventions according to Rome bowel-habit subtype and clinically observable dominant symptoms. Literature was identified through PubMed/MEDLINE and major guidelines, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and pivotal trials published through June 2026. Evidence was interpreted at the level of the exact intervention or product, studied population, target outcome, consistency, independent replication, safety, and guideline position. Mechanistic data support plausible links through fermentation, epithelial barrier function, mucosal immunity, bile-acid metabolism, visceral sensitivity, and gut-brain signaling, but mechanistic or microbiome changes do not establish the clinical efficacy. Rifaximin has the clearest replicated and guideline-supported role in IBS with diarrhea, while soluble fiber has guideline support for global or constipation-associated symptoms. Evidence for individual probiotics, postbiotics, partially hydrolyzed guar gum, galactooligosaccharides, and fermented matrices remains product-specific or emerging and is rarely independently replicated. Symptom improvement with a diet low in fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides, and polyols (low-FODMAP diet) does not establish microbiota mediation. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) and microbiome-guided prescribing remain investigational. Current evidence, therefore, supports only limited phenotype-informed matching and does not establish a validated treatment sequence or microbiome-defined therapeutic phenotype.

articles.title: The cGAS-STING pathway in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: mechanistic insights and therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a highly prevalent chronic metabolic liver disease worldwide, encompassing a spectrum that includes simple steatosis, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), liver fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), with immune-metabolic-inflammatory dysregulation at its core pathogenesis. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway serves as the central axis of cytosolic DNA sensing and innate immune activation. Endogenous stimuli, including mitochondrial DNA leakage, DNA damage, and gut microbial DNA translocation, can persistently activate this pathway, which in turn regulates lipid metabolism imbalance, hepatic inflammation amplification, hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation, and malignant transformation through downstream signaling axes, driving the full spectrum of MASLD pathology. Molecules associated with the cGAS-STING pathway may serve as non-invasive diagnostic biomarkers for MASLD, and natural compounds, traditional Chinese medicine, and nanosystems targeting this pathway have demonstrated promising therapeutic effects. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms of the cGAS-STING pathway, its regulatory roles in MASLD, and advances in targeted therapy, providing a theoretical foundation for disease mechanism elucidation and the development of diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Insights from multi-omics on GLP-1 receptor agonists in type 2 diabetes and obesity.
articles.abstract: Glucagon like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have revolutionized the management of T2D and obesity. T2D clustering highlights distinct phenotypes that differ in GLP-1RA benefit. While they have markedly improved quality of life for many individuals, converging evidence indicates that genetic variation, metabolomic remodeling, and gut microbiota composition contribute to substantial inter-individual variability in GLP-1RA efficacy and tolerability. GLP-1RAs, in return, can variably affect the metabolome and microbiome composition in treated individuals. This review focuses on human multi-omics GLP-1RA intervention studies, complemented by relevant mechanistic preclinical evidence. Genetic variation in GLP1R, TCF7L2, and other loci has been associated with differences in glycaemic and weight outcomes, although most findings remain preliminary, inconsistent across populations, or not yet replicated. Pharmacometabolomic studies show recurrent of lipid-related pathways including, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, ceramides, amino acids, and bile acids, with drug-specific signatures. GLP-1RAs are also associated with changes in gut microbial composition, including taxa such as Akkermansia and Bacteroides, although the direction and clinical significance of these changes vary across studies due to methodological and population heterogeneity. Multi-omics and AI-based models show promise for predicting treatment response by integrating genetic, metabolic, microbial, and clinical data to supporting more effective and individualized therapy and advancing precision medicine.

articles.title: From pathophysiology to therapy: dual and triple agonists as a new frontier in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the most prevalent chronic liver condition worldwide, reflecting the growing global burden of obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D). The complex pathophysiology of MASLD, characterized by insulin resistance (IR), lipotoxicity, and chronic low-grade inflammation, necessitates therapeutic strategies that address systemic metabolic dysfunction rather than isolated hepatic markers. Current evidence highlights the synergistic potential of targeting multiple incretin and metabolic pathways. Dual agonists, most notably Tirzepatide (a GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist), have demonstrated profound efficacy in clinical trials (SURPASS and SURMOUNT programs), achieving significant reductions in hemoglobin A1c, body weight, and liver fat content. Furthermore, dual GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonists like Survodutide and Cotadutide offer complementary benefits by enhancing energy expenditure and modulating hepatic lipid metabolism. The development of triple agonists, such as Retatrutide (targeting GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors), represents a further escalation in potency, showing unprecedented results in liver fat reduction and weight loss. The integration of these multi-target agents, together with emerging pathways involving amylin analogues and pan-PPAR agonists like Chiglitazar, marks a paradigm shift toward holistic cardiometabolic management. These therapies not only target the resolution of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis and fibrosis but also address the interconnected risks of cardiovascular and renal complications. This review aims to explore the evolving landscape of pharmacological interventions, focusing on the emergence of dual and triple receptor agonists as a transformative frontier in metabolic dysfunction and MASLD therapy.

articles.title: Controlling the uncontrollable? navigating naturalistic and controlled dosing in cannabis research.
articles.abstract: Cannabis research is advancing rapidly, yet fundamental questions persist regarding the optimal design of human studies to empirically assess the potential harms and benefits of cannabis. There exist central methodological differences between studies that rely on controlled dose paradigms, ensuring internal validity, and those that utilize naturalistic, self-administration approaches which better reflect real-world use. Controlled paradigms offer precision and regulatory alignment but fail to capture the complexity of real-world cannabis consumption. Naturalistic designs enhance ecological validity but introduce variability and pose challenges for dosing, safety, and replicability. This perspective article presents two methods: one emphasizing the scientific rigor and utility of controlled dose paradigms for regulatory outcomes (e.g., FDA), and the other advocating for naturalistic models that prioritize real-world relevance of legal market cannabis consumption which can inform policy decisions (e.g., guidelines around high THC concentrate). However, rather than representing competing alternatives, controlled laboratory and naturalistic paradigms occupy distinct positions within the evidentiary framework of cannabinoid research, each addressing scientific questions that the other cannot. An integrated methods section proposes ways to incorporate the best features of both approaches to advance cannabinoid science study design.

articles.title: Sustained release of metformin through an injectable hydrogel for synergistic macrophage reprogramming and ROS scavenging in the analgesic treatment of osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA), a prevalent joint disorder affecting millions worldwide, is primarily characterized by chronic pain driven by synovial M1-polarized macrophages, which perpetuate inflammation and generate excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS). However, existing pharmacological treatments offer limited long-term efficacy. Metformin, a known modulator of M1 macrophage polarization and ROS production, has demonstrated efficacy in alleviating OA pain via oral administration. Yet, its therapeutic translation is hindered by poor joint tissue bioavailability. Intra-articular (IA) delivery offers a clinically attractive solution, achieving high local drug concentrations while minimizing systemic exposure, but conventional IA formulations are rapidly cleared from the joint space, restricting their efficacy. We designed an injectable hydrogel based on dopamine (DA) and carboxyl-terminated Pluronic F127 (F127) and crosslinked the hydrogel network via oxidative coupling between catechol groups using an H2O2/horseradish peroxidase (HRP) system (termed 'F127-DA-HRP') to deliver metformin (termed 'Met-F127-DA-HRP') intra-articularly in a sustained manner. The Met-F127-DA-HRP hydrogel scavenges ROS through its catechol groups and sustained metformin release, while also promoting M1-to-M2 macrophage repolarization and suppressing inflammatory cytokines. Importantly, a single IA injection of Met-F127-DA-HRP hydrogel maintained 2-fold higher metformin concentrations in joint tissues compared to Met-F127 hydrogel, with sustained retention for up to 30 days. In monosodium iodoacetate (MIA)-induced OA, IA injection of Met-F127-DA-HRP hydrogel successfully relieved OA pain and ameliorated synovitis with long-lasting effects. Collectively, this work introduces a potent therapeutic strategy for the sustained management of OA pain by utilizing an injectable hydrogel to prolong the IA residency of metformin, offering long-acting IA analgesia through macrophage-directed immunomodulation.

articles.title: Integrating knowledge graphs and retrieval-augmented generation to identify clinical pharmacology gaps in infectious disease trial protocols.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Clinical trial protocols contain critical clinical pharmacology information that is often scattered across different sections of these lengthy documents. The purpose was to evaluate whether a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) protocol review integrated with knowledge graphs (KGs) could be used to obtain clinical pharmacology evidence and identify regulatory gaps. METHODS: Clinical trial protocols were obtained from the Gates Foundation's publicly available corpus of clinical trials in low- and middle-income countries. The RAG protocol review was used to assess the protocols against Food & Drug Administration (FDA) guidance documents for hepatic impairment, exposure-response, population PK (PopPK), and physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling (PBPK). Disease-specific KG analyses were conducted for tuberculosis (TB), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), malaria, and neglected tropical diseases (NTD). KG models connecting studies to drugs, diseases, pharmacologic classes, organ-function exclusions, biomarkers, and pharmacokinetic (PK) parameter features were obtained. RESULTS: Across 42 unique trials, the KG contained 223 nodes and 376 edges. TB protocols produced the largest disease-specific graph, whereas HIV had the highest frequency of PK studies. Gap analysis showed that hepatic impairment exclusions in TB were more frequent than PK studies. In the multi-guidance evaluation, faithfulness was high, answer relevancy was lower, and the clinical pharmacology metric showed guidance-dependent differences. CONCLUSION: The integrated KG-RAG approach can help highlight potential gaps in clinical pharmacology reporting in infectious disease clinical trial protocols.

articles.title: Bioequivalence study of two formulations of a sitagliptin/metformin hydrochloride extended-release tablet in healthy Chinese subjects under fasting and fed conditions: a randomized, open-label, single-dose, crossover trial.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to evaluate the bioequivalence and safety of a newly developed generic sitagliptin/metformin hydrochloride extended-release (XR) tablet (50 mg/500 mg) compared with the reference formulation, Janumet XR, in healthy Chinese subjects under fasting and fed conditions. METHODS: This randomized, open-label, single-dose, two-period, two-sequence crossover study included 40 subjects in the fasting cohort and 36 subjects in the fed cohort. Subjects received a single dose of the test or reference formulation in each period, separated by a 5-day washout period. Plasma concentrations of sitagliptin and metformin were determined using a validated liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry method. Bioequivalence was assessed using the 90% confidence intervals (CIs) for the geometric mean ratios (GMRs; test/reference) of maximum plasma concentration (Cmax), area under the plasma concentration-time curve from time zero to the last quantifiable concentration (AUC0-t), and area under the plasma concentration-time curve from time zero to infinity (AUC0-infinity). RESULTS: Under fasting conditions, the 90% CIs for the GMRs of sitagliptin for Cmax, AUC0-t, and AUC0-infinity were 88.24%-101.46%, 98.24%-103.15%, and 98.41%-103.33%, respectively. The corresponding values for metformin were 93.23%-103.26%, 93.00%-106.20%, and 92.89%-105.74%. Bioequivalence was also established under fed conditions for sitagliptin (Cmax: 88.29%-99.06%; AUC0-t: 96.19%-101.02%; AUC0-infinity: 96.07%-101.04%) and metformin (Cmax: 92.06% -99.39%; AUC0-t: 91.31%-100.06%; AUC0-infinity: 91.00%-99.30%). Analysis of variance showed a significant period effect for metformin AUC0-t and AUC0-infinity under fasting conditions (P < 0.05), whereas no significant formulation effect was observed (P > 0.05). Both formulations were well tolerated. Only Grade 1 or Grade 2 adverse events were reported, and no serious adverse events occurred. DISCUSSION: The generic sitagliptin/metformin hydrochloride XR tablet was bioequivalent to the reference product under both fasting and fed conditions in healthy Chinese subjects. The generic formulation was well tolerated and may provide a safe and effective alternative for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

articles.title: Aloysia deserticola (rica-rica) essential oil impairs inhibitory synaptic transmission in hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons.
articles.abstract: Aloysia deserticola is an aromatic plant native to the Chilean Andean highlands that has traditionally been used in herbal preparations. Although a previous behavioral study reported the anxiolytic and antidepressant-like effects of rica-rica essential oil in an animal model, its neurophysiological actions at cellular and synaptic levels remain largely unexplored. In this study, we characterized A. deserticola essential oil (AD-EO) using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and examined its acute effects on GABAergic synaptic transmission via whole-cell patch-clamp recordings from CA1 pyramidal neurons in acute dorsal hippocampal slices obtained from C57BL/6 J mice. GC-MS analysis revealed an enriched thujone chemical profile, with peaks tentatively identified as α- and β-thujone accounting for 89.06% and 3.38% of the total chromatographic area, respectively. Application of AD-EO to the bath reduced evoked inhibitory postsynaptic current (eIPSC) amplitude in a concentration-dependent manner and shortened eIPSC decay kinetics. This is consistent with a postsynaptic contribution to the suppression of inhibitory signaling. At intermediate-to-high estimated thujone-equivalent concentrations, AD-EO increased the paired-pulse ratio. Coefficient-of-variation analysis supported the presence of an additional presynaptic component. Consistent with these findings, AD-EO reduced the frequency and amplitude of miniature inhibitory postsynaptic currents. Furthermore, the effects on eIPSC amplitude and the paired-pulse ratio were reversible following washout. Together, these results demonstrate that AD-EO suppresses inhibitory synapses in CA1 pyramidal neurons via effects consistent with pre- and postsynaptic locus. These results provide electrophysiological evidence that AD-EO modulates hippocampal inhibitory transmission and support further investigation of the mechanisms underlying the neurophysiological actions of this complex natural preparation.

articles.title: Effect of mucosal hydration on time-dependent mucoadhesion of polymeric nanocomposite microspheres to ovine nasal mucosa: relationship to swelling kinetics.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mucoadhesion of hydrophilic polymeric carriers is strongly influenced by hydration, which promotes polymer-chain mobility and facilitates interactions with mucin. However, excessive hydration may compromise the mechanical integrity of the adhesive interface. This study investigated the temporal relationship between swelling kinetics and nasal mucoadhesion of polymeric nanocomposite microsphere systems under different mucosal hydration conditions. METHODS: Two polymeric nanocomposite microsphere systems, IDB-MS and DFP-MS, were evaluated for swelling over 40 min using standardized compacted microsphere discs and for adhesion to excised ovine nasal mucosa under native/quasi-dry and highly hydrated conditions. Adhesion tension was determined over contact times ranging from 1 to 25 min. The effects of formulation and time on swelling and those of formulation, mucosal hydration, and contact time on adhesion tension were evaluated using factorial ANOVA. RESULTS: Both systems showed comparable swelling kinetics, reaching their maximum experimentally observed swelling at 5 min (465.96% for IDB-MS and 470.00% for DFP-MS), with no significant main effect of formulation. Mucoadhesion was strongly affected by mucosal hydration and contact time, whereas formulation had no significant main effect. Adhesion tension was consistently higher under native/quasi-dry than under highly hydrated mucosal conditions. Spline interpolation estimated the time of maximum adhesion at approximately 4.0-4.5 min, whereas the highest experimentally measured adhesion tension occurred at the 5-min sampling point. However, the post-maximum decline in adhesion preceded the corresponding decrease in apparent swelling, particularly under highly hydrated conditions. CONCLUSION: Polymer swelling and mucoadhesion showed condition-dependent temporal correspondence, but swelling alone was insufficient to explain adhesive strength. The results support the hypothesis that mucoadhesion may depend on a balance between sufficient polymer hydration and preservation of interfacial cohesion; however, the present comparison of two hydration conditions does not establish an optimal hydration level. Mucosal hydration should therefore be considered an important experimental parameter in the evaluation of nasal mucoadhesive drug-delivery systems.

articles.title: Cardiac adverse event signals of Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors as primary suspect and in co-reported regimens: a large-scale FAERS pharmacovigilance study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors (BTKis) have improved outcomes in B-cell malignancies, but cardiac toxicity remains a clinically relevant concern, particularly with newer-generation agents and co-reported regimens. We aimed to characterize real-world cardiac adverse event signals associated with BTKis as primary suspect (PS) agents and in co-reported regimens. METHODS: We conducted a pharmacovigilance study using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System from the fourth quarter of 2013 to the first quarter of 2025. We evaluated BTKi regimens (ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, and zanubrutinib as primary suspect agents) and three specific BTKi-based co-reported combination subgroups (BTKi + anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies, BTKi + venetoclax, and BTKi + lenalidomide). Cardiac adverse events were defined by the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities "Cardiac disorders" system organ class. Disproportionality signals were assessed using four algorithms, and time-to-onset and fatal-case phenotypes were evaluated. RESULTS: A total of 8,266 BTKi-associated cardiac adverse event reports were identified. "Cardiac disorders" showed consistent disproportionality signals across BTKis. Ibrutinib had the broadest cardiac signal spectrum, whereas acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib showed fewer but earlier-onset cardiac events. Median reported time-to-onset was 150 days for ibrutinib, 72.5 days for acalabrutinib, and 66 days for zanubrutinib. Among co-reported regimens, BTKi plus lenalidomide showed the strongest disproportional reporting signal for atrial fibrillation. Reports with fatal cardiac outcome were more frequently reported among males, patients older than 85 years, and events occurring within 30 days of treatment initiation. CONCLUSION: BTKis exhibit distinct real-world cardiac safety profiles. Early cardiovascular surveillance may be particularly important for newer-generation BTKis and BTKi-lenalidomide co-reported regimens, especially in patients with risk factors associated with higher reporting proportions.

articles.title: Blockade of the calpain-1/HSP90/TGF-β1 axis by Astragaloside IV ameliorates bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Previous studies have confirmed the therapeutic potential of Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) in pulmonary fibrosis, yet the upstream regulatory mechanisms governing TGF-β1 stability, particularly involving proteolytic enzymes, are not fully understood. This study investigates the pivotal role of calpain-1 in modulating the HSP90/TGF-β1 signaling pathway, thereby elucidating the effects of AS-IV on bleomycin (BLM)-induced pulmonary fibrosis. METHODS: Calpain-1 knockout (CAPN1-/-) and wild-type (WT) mice were used to establish pulmonary fibrosis models via intratracheal instillation of BLM. Both animal and cell models were administered varying doses of AS-IV for intervention. Inflammatory, oxidative stress, fibrotic, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers were subsequently evaluated. Additionally, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) experiments were employed to assess the binding interactions between AS-IV and the calpain-1/HSP90/TGF-β1 axis. RESULTS: The calpain-1/HSP90/TGF-β1 axis was significantly activated in BLM-induced pulmonary fibrosis mice. AS-IV ameliorated pulmonary fibrosis, EMT, oxidative stress, and inflammation while simultaneously suppressing this overactivated axis. Calpain-1 knockout inhibited HSP90 upregulation, attenuated TGF-β1/Smad2/3 activation, and reduced pulmonary fibrosis. In vivo experiments further confirmed the inhibitory effects of AS-IV and calpain-1 inhibition on lung epithelial cell injury and fibroblast proliferation. Notably, calpain-1 overexpression in MLE-12 cells abolished the protective effects of AS-IV against EMT, oxidative stress, and inflammation. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and SPR experiments confirmed the direct binding between AS-IV and calpain-1, supporting its upstream regulatory role in this signaling axis. CONCLUSION: AS-IV attenuates pulmonary fibrosis by targeting calpain-1 to disrupt the HSP90/TGF-β1 signaling axis. These findings identify calpain-1 as a novel therapeutic target and support AS-IV as a promising candidate for PF treatment.

articles.title: Peptide-Linked Bivalent Nanobody Constructs as Positive Allosteric Modulators of the Calcium-Sensing Receptor.
articles.abstract: We previously developed nanobodies acting as positive allosteric modulators (PAMs) of the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR). Here, we sought to develop more potent CaSR modulators by creating bivalent nanobody constructs using 'tail-to-head' peptide-linker conjugation. The constructs were functionally characterized at CaSR in HEK293 cells in a Ca2+ mobilization assay. Homobivalent Nb4-Nb4 and Nb10-Nb10 constructs with linkers comprising 3, 5, 6 or 9 GGGG(S/T) repeats all displayed CaSR PAM potencies comparable with those exhibited by their monovalent counterparts. Likewise, five heterobivalent nanobodies combining Nb4, Nb10, Nb11, Nb36 or Nb37 through [GGGG(S/T)]9 linkers exhibited PAM potencies similar to that of the monovalent version of the first (N-terminal) nanobody in the respective constructs. This prompted us to examine the functional properties of [GGGG(S/T)]9-linked constructs combining Nb4 and the mGluR5-selective nanobody PAM Nb43mGlu5. Nb4-L9-Nb43mGlu5 displayed slightly increased CaSR PAM potency relative to Nb4, whereas Nb43mGlu5-L9-Nb4 exhibited ~40- and ~10-fold reduced potency compared with Nb4-L9-Nb43mGlu5 and Nb4, respectively. The findings indicate that 'tail-to-head' conjugation markedly reduces CaSR binding affinity of the second (C-terminal) nanobody and likely explains the lack of synergistic enhancement of PAM potency in the bivalent constructs. Thus, the suitability of tail-to-head linker conjugation of nanobodies is context dependent, governed by how the nanobody engages its target and by whether the linker perturbs these interactions.

articles.title: SCN2B Drives Depression-like Phenotypes in Mice by Suppressing BDNF Signaling via Its Intracellular Domain NICD.
articles.abstract: The rising global burden of depression necessitates novel mechanistic insights and therapeutic targets. Voltage-gated sodium channel β2-subunit (Navβ2, coded by SCN2B) has been implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders, yet its role in depression remains unexplored. Here, we identify SCN2B as a previously unrecognized driver of depression-like pathophysiology. Using SCN2B-overexpressing (SCN2B-OV) mice across different ages (1, 12, and 20 months) and CRISPR- engineered Navβ2V173A,V175K mice with selective reduction of the Navβ2 intracellular domain (NICD), we combined behavioral phenotyping, electrophysiology, neurotransmitter profiling, and molecular analyses, with chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) as an environmental challenge. SCN2B-OV mice exhibited accelerated depression-like phenotypes, including anhedonia (sucrose preference 52.42% reduction, P<0.05), behavioral despair (forced swim test immobility 67.42% increase, P<0.05), and cognitive deficits (Y-maze alternation 50.90% reduction, P<0.05), independent of natural aging. Electrophysiologically, SCN2B overexpression induced a striking prefrontal-hippocampal imbalance: prefrontal cortex (PFC) became hyperexcitable (glutamate release increased by 64.7%; sEPSC amplitude increased 2.05-fold, P<0.05), whereas the hippocampus showed synaptic suppression (GABA release reduced by 32.65%; sIPSC frequency reduced by 66.67%, P<0.05). Mechanistically, SCN2B overexpression suppressed BDNF/TrkB/PI3K/AKT signaling axis (BDNF reduced by 53.17%; p-TrkB reduced by 63.62%, P<0.05), accompanied by decreased synaptic proteins (PSD95 43.45%, synapsin I 40.31%, P<0.05). Remarkably, NICD-reduced Navβ2V173A,V175K mice were fully resistant to CUMS-induced behavioral and neurotransmitter deficits, establishing NICD as a critical mediator of stress vulnerability. Collectively, these findings unravel a causal pathway in which SCN2B overexpression drives NICD-dependent suppression of BDNF signaling, leading to region-specific excitatory/inhibitory imbalance, synaptic disintegration, and depression-like phenotypes. Targeting Navβ2 proteolysis to block NICD generation may thus represent a novel therapeutic strategy for mood disorders.

articles.title: 3,4-Dimethoxyacetophenone ameliorates epileptogenesis by suppressing BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/ STAT-3 expression in a pentylenetetrazole-induced kindling model of epilepsy.
articles.abstract: Epilepsy is a neurological condition that affects approximately 50 million individuals worldwide. Current treatments mainly alleviate symptoms and have substantial adverse effects, with about 1/3 of patients not responding to existing medications. This underscores the urgent need for new drugs that can overcome these challenges. According to recent studies, the Janus kinase/ signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/ STAT) pathway play an important role in epileptogenesis. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and c-fos are also involved in neuronal excitability and seizure-induced neuronal changes. The purpose of the present study was to examine the anticonvulsant and antiepileptogenic activities of 3,4-dimethoxyacetophenone (3,4-DMA) in the acute seizure and pentylenetetrazole (PTZ)-induced kindling models of epilepsy and to elucidate related molecular changes of BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/ STAT-3 signaling pathways. 3,4-DMA was first evaluated in an acute seizure model, followed by a kindling model of epilepsy in mice. The effects of 3,4-DMA on BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/ STAT-3 were assessed by quantitative reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) and immunohistochemistry (IHC). The results showed that 3,4-DMA significantly reduced seizure scores in a PTZ-induced kindling model. BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/ STAT-3 were significantly upregulated in both the cortical and hippocampal tissues in PTZ-control mice. Conversely, treatment with 3,4-DMA attenuated this overexpression in the cortex and hippocampus. In conclusion, 3,4-DMA has antiepileptogenic effect as evidenced by a reduction in the expression of BDNF, c-fos and the JAK-2/ STAT-3 pathway components. So, it can be a promising therapeutic candidate in the treatment of epilepsy. However, future studies measuring p-JAK-2 and p-STAT-3 will be required to confirm pathway activation status.

articles.title: Ligand-specific effects of 5-HT2A receptor antagonists on fear extinction in C57BL/6J mice: Comparative insights from MDL 11,939 and MDL 100,907.
articles.abstract: Serotonin (5-HT) 2A receptors (5-HT2AR) modulate corticolimbic circuits underlying fear extinction, but the behavioral consequences of 5-HT2AR antagonism during extinction remain poorly defined. Here, we examined the systemic effects of the 5-HT2A/2C antagonist MDL 11,939 (Glemanserin) and the selective 5-HT2A antagonist MDL 100,907 (Volinanserin) on fear extinction in adult female and male C57BL/6J mice. Prior to drug administration, mice acquired comparable conditioned freezing responses during delay fear conditioning. Twenty-four hours later, acute administration of MDL 11,939 (1.0 mg/kg) or MDL 100,907 (0.01 mg/kg) increased freezing to the first conditioned stimulus (CS) presentation on Extinction Day 1 in males, indicating enhanced expression of conditioned fear. Repeated administration of MDL 11,939 significantly impaired extinction in male mice, evidenced by increased freezing across extinction trials and an increased number of trials required to reach extinction criterion. Neither acute nor repeated MDL 11,939 altered extinction in female mice. In males, MDL 100,907 produced a transient increase in freezing during extinction but did not delay extinction acquisition and had no effect in females. Because MDL 11,939 has reported affinity for 5-HT2C receptors, we tested potential contributions of 5-HT2C receptor antagonism in a separate cohort of male mice given repeated administration of the selective 5-HT2C antagonist SB 242084 (0.25 or 0.5 mg/kg). Neither dose affected conditioned fear expression, extinction learning, or trials required to reach extinction criterion. Together, these findings demonstrate ligand-, sex-, and dose-dependent effects of 5-HT2AR antagonism on fear extinction and suggest that distinct intracellular receptor signaling mechanisms may differentially regulate extinction-related behavior.

articles.title: Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate exacerbates psoriasis-like skin inflammation and is associated with interleukin-17A signaling and S100A9/FABP5 upregulation in keratinocytes.
articles.abstract: Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) is a ubiquitous environmental contaminant that has been implicated in immune and inflammatory dysregulation, but its potential role in psoriasis-related skin inflammation remains unclear. In this study, we integrated bioinformatics, network toxicology, and machine-learning analyses to identify candidate genes associated with DEHP-exacerbated psoriasis-like inflammation, followed by experimental validation in in vivo and in vitro models. Public transcriptomic datasets were analyzed to screen differentially expressed genes and prioritize key candidates. S100A9 and FABP5 were identified as high-priority genes by machine learning and were further examined in an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasis-like mouse model and in DEHP-treated HaCaT keratinocytes. Our results showed that DEHP exposure exacerbated IMQ-induced psoriasiform skin inflammation in mice and was associated with increased expression of S100A9, FABP5, and IL-17A-related inflammatory markers in mouse skin. In HaCaT cells, DEHP treatment was also associated with increased S100A9/FABP5 expression under the tested conditions. These exploratory findings suggest that DEHP exposure may exacerbate psoriasis-like skin inflammation and is associated with increased keratinocyte S100A9/FABP5 expression and IL-17A-related signaling. Translation to human psoriasis remains uncertain. Further functional studies are needed to clarify the causal role and mechanistic significance of this pathway.

articles.title: Insights into CD36/P-gp involvement in dietary lipid-driven PAH transport across the blood-brain barrier.
articles.abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), as widespread environmental contaminants, exhibit neurotoxicity. Because PAHs often co-occur with dietary lipids in foods, those lipids might serve as vehicles that alter PAH biotransport and accumulation in the brain. In this work, we systematically investigated how three common dietary fatty acids-oleic acid, linoleic acid (LA), and linolenic acid-differently influence the transport steps (including cellular uptake, efflux, and clearance) of benzo[a]pyrene (BaP) and benzo[b]fluoranthene (BbF) across the blood-brain barrier, using a bEnd.3 cell-based model, and explored the potential underlying molecular mechanisms. Results revealed that dietary lipids, acting as carriers, significantly enhanced cellular uptake of PAHs, with LA increasing the uptake of BaP and BbF by 20.36% and 17.90%, respectively, and accelerated transmembrane transport dynamics. Simultaneously, distinct lipids differentially affected PAH clearance and efflux. Notably, LA delayed the clearance of PAHs, prolonging the elimination half-life of BaP from 10.117 h to 17.696 h and that of BbF from 7.418 h to 14.964 h, thereby increasing overall brain exposure. Mechanistically, LA was observed to upregulate the fatty acid transporter CD36, and functional inhibition studies suggested that P-glycoprotein and CD36 may jointly contribute to lipid-modulated effects. This study suggests that dietary lipids influence brain exposure to PAHs through a multi-level network, highlighting a factor that warrants consideration when assessing their neurotoxicity risks.

articles.title: Enhanced inhalation delivery of ROS-responsive methylprednisolone dimer nanoparticles via hydrogen-oxygen carrier gas for efficient treatment of acute lung injury with CFD-simulated pulmonary deposition.
articles.abstract: Distal lung delivery remains a key bottleneck for inhaled therapy in severe pulmonary disease. We developed a hydrogen-oxygen mixture (H2/O2 mixture, 2:1 v/v) gas-assisted nebulization platform to deliver ROS-responsive, self-assembled methylprednisolone dimer nanoparticles (MP2-TK NPs). MP2-TK NPs were stable during nebulization and selectively released drug under ROS-rich conditions. Compared with air, H2/O2 mixture improved NGI-assessed aerosol deposition and artificial mucus penetration. CFD simulations further supported enhanced distal deposition, particularly for clinically respirable droplets (1-5 μm). In an LPS-induced acute lung injury mouse model, H2/O2-assisted nebulization increased pulmonary distribution and small-airway localization of MP2-TK NPs, leading to reduced bronchoalveolar lavage cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β), total cell counts, and protein levels. H2/O2 mixture inhalation alone also showed anti-inflammatory activity, consistent with hydrogen's antioxidant effects. This strategy couples carrier-gas engineering with ROS-responsive nanomedicine to enhance deep-lung delivery and therapeutic efficacy in acute lung injury.

articles.title: Magnetic stirring-assisted wet milling of imatinib-curcumin drug-drug nanococrystals: preparation, characterization, dissolution and intravenous pharmacokinetics.
articles.abstract: Drug-drug cocrystals offer a promising strategy for developing fixed-dose combination formulations by integrating multiple active pharmaceutical ingredients into a single crystalline lattice. However, their application may be limited by insufficient dissolution improvement and the relatively large particle sizes of conventional cocrystals. Herein, an imatinib-curcumin drug-drug nanococrystal (nano-IM-CUR) was prepared by combining cocrystallization with nanonization to investigate its apparent dissolution behavior and pharmacokinetic performance following intravenous administration in rats. A wet-milling strategy assisted by magnetic stirring was established, and formulation and process parameters were systematically optimized. The optimized nano-IM-CUR exhibited an average particle size of approximately 200 nm, a narrow size distribution, and good reproducibility. Solid-state characterization confirmed that the original cocrystal phase was retained after nanonization. Compared with the micron-sized cocrystal, nano-IM-CUR exhibited higher apparent plateau concentrations of IM and CUR under the tested non-sink dissolution conditions. The nanococrystal suspension showed limited changes in particle size and PDI during 180 days of storage at 4 and 25 °C under the tested conditions. Following intravenous administration in rats, both IM and CUR were detected in plasma. This study provides an equipment-accessible wet-milling strategy for converting the micron-sized IM-CUR drug-drug cocrystal into a nanosized suspension while retaining its characteristic cocrystal phase.

articles.title: The photostability of ketamine products: part ii impact of light exposure and storage on multi-use ketamine parenteral products.
articles.abstract: Ketamine drug products for parenteral use are commonly packaged in multi-use clear glass vials. However, light exposure may cause formation of N-nitroso-ketamine (NNKet), a potential carcinogen and nitrosamine drug substance-related impurity (NDSRI) of regulatory concern. To better understand ketamine photostability and nitrosamine formation potential, a photostability investigation was performed using a two-stage approach evaluating ambient and intense light exposure followed by post-exposure storage. This design reflects clinical reality where multi-use injectable ketamine experiences multiple intermittent light exposures during use. A selective and sensitive UHPLC-MS/MS analytical procedure was developed and validated for NNKet quantification. Sample preparation required solid phase extraction (SPE) to separate NNKet from ketamine before LC-MS/MS measurement, essential for overcoming autosampler contamination and ionization suppression from million-fold excess ketamine. Unexpectedly, NNKet concentration initially decreased during light exposure but rapidly increased during post-exposure storage. NNKet increased from baseline levels of approximately 5 ng/mL and exceeded the lowest acceptable intake limit of 14 ng/mL for 10 mg/mL ketamine drug product, reaching 100 ng/mL in some cases within 8 weeks of post-exposure storage. Control samples (light-protected vials) showed minimal NNKet change (maximum increase of 4.7 ng/mL from baseline). Kinetic modeling and experiments were attempted to explain the underlying mechanism. These findings demonstrate a post-market safety concern for ketamine drug products stored in clear glass vials, suggesting that container-closure systems minimizing light exposure, such as amber glass vials, may help mitigate nitrosamine formation risks in ketamine drug products.

articles.title: Elimination profile of dexamethasone in dried blood spots (DBS) following single and multiple oral administration and proposal of the minimum reporting level to distinguish forbidden from allowed administrations in sports drug testing.
articles.abstract: Glucocorticoids (GC), such as dexamethasone (DEX), are prohibited in sports competitions when administered by systemic routes including oral, injectable, and rectal administrations. Since they remain permitted by other therapeutic routes, Minimum Reporting Levels (MRLs) are required to detect misuse in sports. Although antidoping analyses are mainly performed in urine, increasing interest has recently focused on alternative matrices such as dried blood spots (DBS). In this study, the suitability of DBS for the detection of DEX and the evaluation of its elimination profile was investigated. A liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry method was developed for the quantification of DEX and its main metabolite, 6β-hydroxy-DEX, in DBS. The method showed good linearity, sensitivity, precision, and accuracy, with no significant matrix effects. It was applied to samples collected after oral administration of DEX in healthy male participants following single-dose (4 mg, n=8) and multiple-dose (2 × 2 mg/day for 5 days, n=8) regimens. DEX and its metabolite reached the highest concentrations within the first 4 h post-administration and were generally detectable up to 24 h, without evidence of accumulation after repeated dosing. Cortisol suppression was observed in all participants, confirming the systemic effect of oral DEX administration. Plasma samples collected at the same time points showed similar concentration profiles, suggesting homogeneous distribution of DEX between plasma and red blood cells. Based on the DBS-to-plasma ratio obtained and literature plasma data, an MRL of 2 ng/mL in DBS was proposed to identify prohibited systemic DEX administration during sports competitions.

articles.title: Alginate Oligosaccharide Alleviates Age-Related Hearing Loss via TFEB-Associated Autophagy Restoration to Attenuate Oxidative Stress and Inflammation.
articles.abstract: Age-related hearing loss (ARHL) is a highly prevalent sensory disorder characterized by progressive cochlear degeneration. To date, no effective pharmacological treatment is clinically available. In this study, we investigated the otoprotective efficacy and underlying mechanisms of alginate oligosaccharide (AOS) against D-galactose (D-gal)-induced senescence in vitro and age-associated cochlear dysfunction in C57BL/6J mice. Multi-omics analyses identified oxidative stress, inflammation, cellular senescence, and autophagy, as core targeted pathways associated with AOS treatment. In D-gal-treated HEI-OC1 cells and cochlear explants, AOS treatment markedly reduced senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) activity and downregulated senescence markers P16 and P21. These anti-senescent effects were accompanied by ameliorated oxidative and pro-inflammatory stress, as reflected by decreased reactive oxygen species (ROS), preserved mitochondrial function, and suppressed nuclear factor-κB/NOD-like receptor pyrin domain-containing 3 (NF-κB/NLRP3) signaling. AOS also promoted transcription factor EB (TFEB) nuclear translocation and attenuated D-gal-induced autophagy-related dysregulation. Pharmacological inhibition of autophagy and TFEB nuclear entry effectively blunted these cytoprotective, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory benefits of AOS, supporting the involvement of TFEB-associated autophagic signaling in AOS-mediated protection. In C57BL/6J mice, long-term AOS administration significantly lowered auditory brainstem response (ABR) thresholds, attenuated the age-related degeneration of hair cells and spiral ganglion neurons, and reduced cochlear senescence markers. Furthermore, AOS suppressed MDA accumulation, elevated SOD activity, inhibited NF-κB/NLRP3 activation, and restored TFEB-associated autophagic homeostasis in vivo. Collectively, these findings suggest that AOS protects against age-associated cochlear dysfunction and senescence, accompanied by reduced oxidative stress and inflammation and improved autophagy-related homeostasis. TFEB-associated signaling may contribute to these protective effects, supporting further investigation of AOS for the prevention or delay of cochlear aging.

articles.title: Evaluating Kinetic Solubility - A Comparative Study of Analytical Approaches Using UV-based Evaluation Methods.
articles.abstract: Supersaturation-based formulation strategies are widely used to enhance the oral bioavailability of poorly water-soluble drugs, yet the accurate identification of precipitation onset (kinetic solubility) remains method-dependent and poorly standardized. In this study, the kinetic solubility of eight model compounds was systematically investigated using in situ UV spectroscopy and dynamic light scattering (DLS), with UV data evaluated using baseline elevation, second-derivative analysis, and the zero-intercept method (ZIM). Baseline elevation and second-derivative approaches showed strong agreement, detecting precipitation at similar concentrations corresponding to the formation of optically detectable particles. In contrast, ZIM consistently identified transitions at lower concentrations, indicating higher sensitivity to early aggregation events. DLS measurements confirmed the presence of particles at concentrations corresponding to ZIM-detected endpoints, supporting its association with the initial stages of phase separation. In some cases, liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) was observed, with ZIM detecting early phase transitions prior to visible liquid droplets. Comparative statistical analysis proved that the second derivative and baseline methods provided the highest repeatability (within-unit %CV 3.5% and 4.8%, respectively), whereas ZIM-based approaches showed greater variability despite their higher sensitivity. The combination of ZIM and DLS provides a more comprehensive understanding of the onset of precipitation and supersaturation behaviour of poorly soluble drugs, supporting improved characterization and kinetic solubility evaluation in early formulation development.

articles.title: cGAS-STING activation promotes abdominal aortic aneurysm formation in mice and humans: Therapeutic potential of inhibition.
articles.abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease lacking effective pharmacotherapy. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) innate immune pathway has been linked to inflammatory conditions, yet its role in AAA remains unclear. Here, we combined single-cell transcriptomics, mouse models, pharmacological inhibition, and human tissue validation to investigate the role of this pathway in AAA. In murine single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data, cGAS-STING activation was predominantly observed in AAA endothelial cells (ECs). Human scRNA-seq and scissor-based classification of stable versus ruptured AAAs showed that cGAS and STING1 were significantly upregulated in ECs from ruptured AAA, implicating pathway activation in rupture risk. Bioinformatic analyses suggested that endothelial cGAS-STING activation correlates with barrier dysfunction and oxidative stress, and that dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) deficiency may link DNA damage to pathway activation. In Angiotensin II (Ang II) -induced murine AAA, cGAS, p-STING, and p-TBK1 were markedly elevated. Pharmacological blockade with RU.521 (cGAS inhibitor) or STING-IN-2 (STING antagonist) reduced AAA incidence, aortic dilation, and structural damage, while improving endothelial mitochondrial morphology. In human AAA tissues, immunohistochemistry (IHC) confirmed increased cGAS, STING, and TBK1 expression. Moreover, RU.521 or STING-IN-2 treatment of patient-derived 3D AAA organoids significantly downregulated cGAS, p-STING, and p-TBK1, confirming target engagement. Collectively, our findings indicate that the cGAS-STING pathway is activated in murine and human AAA, and that targeting this axis may offer a promising therapeutic approach to limit AAA progression.

articles.title: Gramine limits alcohol-associated liver injury by suppressing NOX1-linked ferroptotic responses and mitochondrial dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Alcohol-associated liver injury involves oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ferroptosis-related damage. NADPH oxidase 1 (NOX1), together with its regulatory GTPase Ras-related C3 botulinum toxin substrate 1 (RAC1), forms a regulatory module that governs redox signaling. Yet small molecules that engage NOX1 and suppress these coupled injury programs remain insufficiently defined. Here, we identified gramine as a candidate NOX1-engaging compound and delineated its protective mechanism in ethanol-associated hepatocellular injury. Alcohol challenge induced a hepatic NOX1/RAC1 response, recapitulated in ethanol-injured hepatocytes. Silencing Nox1 or Rac1 blunted ethanol-driven injury phenotypes, limiting injury-associated enzyme release, reactive oxygen species accumulation, mitochondrial membrane potential disturbance, mitochondrial network disruption, and DNA fragmentation while partially preserving glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4). Molecular docking predicted a gramine-NOX1 interaction, a cellular thermal shift assay supported target engagement, and cycloheximide chase analysis showed gramine accelerated NOX1 protein turnover. In ethanol-exposed hepatocytes, gramine conferred concentration-associated protection, improving cell viability, and reducing injury-associated enzyme release, lipid droplet signals, and DNA fragmentation. Post-ethanol gramine treatment reduced injury-associated enzyme release. NOX1 overexpression undermined gramine-mediated protection and reinstated ferrous iron accumulation, glutathione redox imbalance, reactive oxygen species production, mitochondrial dysfunction, and damage-associated signaling. Erastin weakened gramine-mediated protection, implicating inhibition of ferroptotic responses in the protective mechanism. In alcohol-gavaged mice, gramine reduced hepatic NOX1 abundance, serum injury markers, Fe2+ levels, lipid accumulation, and lipid peroxidation-associated changes, while preserving GPX4 abundance and limiting histopathological injury. These findings support gramine as a NOX1-engaging small molecule that limits alcohol-associated liver injury by suppressing NOX1-linked ferroptotic responses and mitochondrial dysfunction.

articles.title: D14, a β-carboline alkaloid derivative of dehydrocrenatidine, exerts anti-glioma effect by targeting SRC.
articles.abstract: Gliomas are malignant tumors of the central nervous system, which urgently require new drugs or treatment methods. It was found that dehydrocrenatidine (DEC), a β-carboline alkaloid isolated from Picrasma quassioides, had good antitumor activity, including against gliomas. This study designed the total DEC synthesis route, and the gram-level yield reached about 49%. To obtain more active β-carboline derivatives, we modified the N1 and C3/C6/C10 positions, producing nineteen compounds (D1-D19), which were screened in six glioma cell types, including three types of clinical primary cells. D14 had the best cytotoxicity, and induced significant apoptosis and oxidative stress in glioma cells. Virtual screening predicted D14 possibly targeting the proto-oncogene tyrosine-protein kinase Src (SRC) to exert an anti-tumor effect. Molecular dynamics and CETSA verified D14 binding to SRC at the site of Gln147, inhibiting the phosphorylation of SRC in glioma cells. Mechanistically, D14 markedly suppressed the PI3K/AKT and STAT3 signaling pathways. D14 significantly inhibited tumor growth without functional toxicity to other normal organs in the model of orthotopically transplanted GL261 tumor cells. Post-D14 treatment in vivo p-SRC levels declined prominently. In conclusion, this study elucidated the potential mechanism of action of the β-carboline alkaloid derivative D14 against glioma and provided a theoretical and scientific basis for glioma prevention and treatment.

articles.title: Withaferin A induces apoptosis and ferroptosis in gastric cancer cells via ROS-mediated mitochondrial damage and the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 axis.
articles.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide with a high mortality rate, and conventional chemotherapy faces significant limitations due to drug resistance and severe adverse effects. Natural products represent promising alternative therapeutic agents. In this study, withaferin A (WA), a major bioactive compound derived from Withania somnifera, was investigated for its anticancer activity in GC. We found that WA inhibited the growth and migration of GC cells while inducing both apoptosis and ferroptosis. WA dose-dependently suppressed GC cell proliferation and colony formation. Mechanistically, WA induced apoptosis through ROS accumulation, resulting in mitochondrial depolarization, increased expression of BAX/BAD, and decreased expression of Bcl-2. Meanwhile, WA triggered ferroptosis by promoting ubiquitin-dependent degradation of GPX4, depleting GSH, increasing lipid peroxidation and MDA levels, and activating the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling axis to elevate Fe2⁺ accumulation. Western blotting and transcriptomic analysis further demonstrated that WA regulated apoptosis- and ferroptosis-related proteins and activated the Keap1/Nrf2 pathway. In vivo, WA significantly suppressed tumor growth in a xenograft model without causing apparent systemic toxicity, indicating its therapeutic potential for GC treatment.
