Collectively, these findings demonstrate that withaferin A is a potent and promising natural compound that induces apoptosis and ferroptosis in gastric cancer cells through ROS-mediated mitochondrial damage and the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 signaling pathway, respectively, highlighting its potential as a candidate therapeutic agent for cancer treatment.

articles.title: Evaluation of the minipig as an alternative model based on cross-study comparisons with rabbit in mRNA vaccine safety assessment.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Robust non-clinical safety models are crucial to the development and evaluation of messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA)-based drugs and vaccines. In this study, we leveraged cross-study data to explore whether the Göttingen minipig could serve as an alternative to the rabbit, a commonly used species in vaccine safety assessment. METHODS: Results from two independent toxicity studies of lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated mRNA encoding the hemagglutinin H3 antigen, administered at equivalent dose levels, were qualitatively compared. Clinical observations, local reactions, body weight, food consumption, body temperature, clinical pathology, immunogenicity, inflammatory biomarkers, and anatomical pathology endpoints were evaluated. RESULTS: Both species exhibited expected vaccine responses, with minor differences in local reactogenicity and body temperature. The vaccine candidate was well tolerated at the injection site in both species. However, mild and transient vaccine-related effects (i.e., injection site induration and increased body temperature) were observed only in minipigs. Transient increases in neutrophil, fibrinogen, and C-reactive protein levels were observed in both species following vaccination, consistent with an inflammatory response. Microscopic findings (i.e., inflammation at the injection site and increased germinal center cellularity in the draining lymph nodes) were comparable between species and aligned with expected immune activation following vaccination. CONCLUSIONS: This qualitative comparison provides preliminary, supportive evidence for the potential use of the minipig as an alternative to the rabbit in non-clinical safety evaluation of mRNA vaccines, with the added benefit of larger blood volume for sampling and availability of validated key inflammatory markers.

articles.title: Naringin attenuates melamine-induced renal biochemical alterations in rats: Histopathological and immunohistochemical assessment.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Naringin has shown nephroprotective activity in several toxicant models. This study evaluated renal outcomes during concurrent naringin administration and repeated melamine exposure. METHODS: Thirty Sprague-Dawley rats were allocated to five groups, each containing three males and three females: control, naringin alone (100 mg/kg/day), melamine alone (300 mg/kg/day), and melamine plus naringin (50 or 100 mg/kg/day). Treatment continued orally for 28 days. We assessed serum creatinine, urea, and uric acid; renal superoxide dismutase activity; tumor necrosis factor-α concentrations; histopathology; and 15A3 immunoreactivity. Factorial models used individual SOD values and rounded group means, standard deviations, and sample sizes for the other biochemical outcomes to estimate treatment contrasts averaged equally across sexes. Tissue-score frequencies were summarized descriptively. RESULTS: Treatment-group effects were significant for all five biochemical outcomes (all p < 0.001). Compared with melamine alone, the 100 mg/kg naringin regimen was associated with a sex-balanced mean creatinine difference of -0.640 mg/dL (Tukey-adjusted 95% CI -0.809 to -0.471). Both naringin regimens showed partial attenuation of the measured biochemical abnormalities, with larger differences at 100 mg/kg. These contrasts remained significant in a heteroscedastic sensitivity analysis. Renal SOD activity was higher than with melamine alone but remained below control values. Selected within-sex pairwise comparisons of H&E injury scores and 15A3 staining categories among the melamine-only and two co-treatment groups were not significant after Holm adjustment (all adjusted p ≥ 0.300). Separate weekly treatment-group comparisons of body weight were not significant. CONCLUSIONS: Concurrent naringin administration was associated with partial attenuation of the measured biochemical abnormalities during melamine exposure. The selected pairwise analyses did not establish differences in H&E injury or 15A3 staining categories among the melamine-only and co-treatment groups. These findings do not establish recovery of renal filtration or tubular function. Small samples, summary-data inference, and antibody specificity limit conclusions about sex differences and DNA-specific injury.

articles.title: Phenylboronic acid-functionalised gelatin/PVA films for enhanced vaginal mucoadhesion and sustained metronidazole release.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop gelatin films with enhanced mucoadhesive retention and controlled metronidazole (MTZ) release for vaginal drug delivery. Gelatin was functionalised with 4-formylphenylboronic acid (FPBA) via Schiff base formation followed by reductive amination to obtain derivatives with different functionalisation levels (Gel-Bor L, Gel-Bor M and Gel-Bor H). Structural changes in gelatin were confirmed by 1H NMR and FTIR spectroscopy, while pH-dependent electrophoretic mobility revealed a shift in the isoelectric point towards lower pH values following derivatisation. Films were prepared by solvent casting using PVA as a film-forming excipient and characterised in terms of thickness, surface pH, folding endurance, transparency, thermal stability and puncture resistance. Ex vivo mucoadhesion of NaFl-loaded films was assessed on freshly excised sheep vaginal mucosa using a flow-through wash-off assay in vaginal fluid simulant (VFS, pH 4.0). In vitro MTZ release was evaluated using Franz diffusion cells, while cytocompatibility was assessed in HT-29 cells and MSCs using the CCK-8 assay. Gel-Bor/PVA films were uniform, flexible and compatible with simulated vaginal pH. Compared with PVA-only and gelatin/PVA controls, Gel-Bor/PVA films exhibited markedly improved mucosal retention, with Gel-Bor L/PVA and Gel-Bor M/PVA performing comparably to chitosan. Chemical modification of gelatin also prolonged MTZ release: after 16 h, cumulative release decreased from 73.10% for gelatin/PVA to 66.50%, 60.40% and 51.70% for Gel-Bor L/PVA, Gel-Bor M/PVA and Gel-Bor H/PVA, respectively. No cytotoxic effects were detected under the tested conditions for all Gel-Bor/PVA formulations. Overall, this chemical modification transformed gelatin-based films into mucoadhesive, cytocompatible platforms with sustained MTZ release for vaginal application.

articles.title: Synergistic lubrication of trazodone hydrochloride by magnesium stearate and Syloid: Critical role of mixing sequence.
articles.abstract: Sticking of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) to punches and dies remains a significant challenge in direct compression, particularly for highly adhesive compounds such as trazodone hydrochloride. This study investigated influence of lubricant type, premix design, and mixing sequence on lubrication efficiency and sticking mitigation. Binary mixtures containing trazodone hydrochloride and either magnesium stearate or amorphous porous silica (Syloid) were compared with ternary systems combining both excipients. Magnesium stearate provided effective boundary lubrication and markedly reduced sticking propensity, whereas Syloid alone showed poor lubrication efficiency and in some cases increased sticking behavior. Conversely, ternary systems exhibited strong dependence on the order of component incorporation. SEM/EDS analysis revealed Syloid can preferentially occupy API surfaces when introduced during early mixing stages, limiting access of magnesium stearate to critical interfacial regions and reducing lubrication efficiency. Conversely, premixing strategies favoring early adsorption of magnesium stearate promoted formation of effective lubrication layer and resulted in synergistically improved compaction performance. Surface etching experiments indicated pressure-dependent redistribution of magnesium stearate during compaction, consistent with its pronounced plastic deformability. Findings demonstrate lubrication efficiency is determined not only by lubricant selection but also by sequence-dependent microstructural organization established during premixing, highlighting premix design as a critical parameter for mitigating sticking.

articles.title: Can deep eutectic mixtures affect the skin permeation and rheological behavior of thermoresponsive hydrogels? A case study with ibuprofen.
articles.abstract: Ibuprofen (IBU) is widely used for the topical treatment of inflammatory disorders; however, its tendency to crystallize in aqueous vehicles and limited cutaneous permeation pose significant formulation challenges. Then, the formation of an ibuprofen-menthol deep eutectic mixture (EM) and subsequent incorporation into thermoresponsive hydrogels based on Poloxamers 407/188 was considered in this new study. The effect of the EM on the hydrogel gelation temperature and time, rheological behavior, viscosity, spreadability and cutaneous permeation was evaluated. Hydrogels containing the EM led to a significant reduction in gelation temperature (25.67-29.67°C vs. 38.00°C for the control), faster sol-gel transition (118.67-153.33 s), increased gel strength and viscosity, suggesting stronger micellar interactions within the poloxamer network. Despite the higher viscosity, EM hydrogels achieved a nearly twofold increase in cumulative IBU permeation compared to the control, which was associated with improved drug solubilization and the permeation-enhancing effect of menthol. In summary, the incorporation of the EM into hydrogels presenting emulsifying properties proved to be an effective approach for overcoming biopharmaceutical issues, beside improving gel properties and simplifying the production process. Given the benefits achieved, this approach could also be explored for other poorly water-soluble molecules to be incorporated into aqueous topical formulations, ensuring substantial advances in this field.

articles.title: Jinfeng Pills Ameliorate Levonorgestrel-Induced Ovarian Injury by Modulating ApoA1-Associated Cholesterol Homeostasis and PI3K/Akt Signaling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Jinfeng Pills (JFP, NMPA approval No. Z20064400) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula clinically used to regulate menstruation and support ovulation. It consists of nine medicinal materials: Epimedium brevicornu Maxim. (Yinyanghuo), Cervus elaphus Linnaeus (Lurong), Panax ginseng C.A.Mey. (Renshen), Equus asinus (EJiao), Ligustrum lucidum W.T.Aiton (Nvzhenzi), Reynoutria multiflora (Thunb.) Moldenke (Heshouwu), Curculigo orchioides Gaertn. (Xianmao), Cinnamomum cassia (L.) J.Presl (Rougui) and Leonurus japonicus Houtt. (Yimucao). Previous studies have demonstrated the protective effects of JFP against ovarian dysfunction. However, the potential protective effects of JFP against ovarian injury induced by chronic exposure to levonorgestrel (LNG), a progestin commonly used in emergency contraception, and their underlying mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of JFP against ovarian injury induced by chronic LNG exposure and to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A rat model of chronic LNG exposure was established, and the efficacy of JFP was evaluated based on estrous cycles, serum hormone levels and ovarian morphology. Ovarian transcriptomic analysis and cholesterol-related biochemical assays were performed to investigate the alterations in ovarian cholesterol homeostasis. The role of apolipoprotein A-I (ApoA1) was further examined by using ApoA1 silencing in primary rat ovarian theca cells and intrabursal administration of ApoA1 in vivo. RT-qPCR and Western blotting were subsequently used to validate the key molecular changes and assess the effects of JFP on ApoA1expression, cholesterol homeostasis and the associated signaling pathways. RESULTS: JFP significantly ameliorated LNG-induced ovarian injury, as evidenced by increased serum levels of FSH, LH and AMH, and decreased estradiol levels and the LH/FSH ratio, reduced cystic follicle formation, and attenuated follicular depletion. Transcriptomic analysis in ovarian tissues, together with cholesterol assays, RT-qPCR and Western blotting, revealed that LNG exposure disrupted ovarian cholesterol homeostasis, with alterations in cholesterol transport and increased ovarian ApoA1 abundance. Intrabursal administration of ApoA1 induced ovarian pathological changes and activated PI3K/Akt signaling in vivo, whereas ApoA1 silencing attenuated PI3K/Akt activation and inhibited the viability of primary ovarian theca cells. JFP markedly reduced ovarian ApoA1 accumulation, improved cholesterol homeostasis, and suppressed PI3K/Akt/NF-κB signaling. CONCLUSION: JFP effectively ameliorated ovarian injury induced by long-term LNG exposure in rats, and its protective effects were likely associated with modulation of ApoA1-associated cholesterol homeostasis and suppression of PI3K/Akt signaling.

articles.title: Chaihu-Shugan-San Attenuates Depression by Downregulating Liver LCN2 to Suppress LHb GluN2B-Associated Glutamatergic Signaling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The liver-brain axis has emerged as a critical pathway in depression pathogenesis, yet the molecular basis of this crosstalk remains largely unexplored. Chaihu-Shugan-San (CSS), a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine formula for "soothing the liver and relieving depression" has shown both hepatoprotective and antidepressant effects, but whether these actions are linked via the liver-brain axis and through what molecular mechanism remains unknown. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to determine whether Chaihu-Shugan-San (CSS) exerts antidepressant effects via the liver-brain axis and to elucidate the mediating role of liver lipocalin 2 (LCN2) and its receptor SLC22A17 in regulating lateral habenula (LHb) function. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model was established. CSS (2, 4, 8 g/kg) or fluoxetine (10 mg/kg) was orally administered. Depressive-like behaviors were assessed by sucrose preference, open field, and forced swim tests. Hepatic injury was evaluated by serum ALT/AST and H&E staining. Liver transcriptomics and LHb single-cell RNA sequencing were performed to identify key molecules, followed by qRT-PCR, Western blot, ELISA, and immunofluorescence for validation. The causal role of LCN2 was tested via liver-specific AAV-mediated overexpression. RESULTS: CSS ameliorated CUMS-induced depressive-like behaviors and liver injury. Transcriptomics and PPI network analysis identified Lcn2 as a hub gene. CSS reversed CUMS-induced elevation of LCN2 in the liver, serum, and LHb, as well as the upregulation of its receptor SLC22A17 in the LHb. LHb single-cell sequencing revealed that CSS restored CUMS-induced changes in astrocyte subcluster ASC6, including downregulation of AQP4 and SLC38A1 and impaired intercellular communication. Consequently, CSS reduced the elevated expression of c-FOS and GluN2B and restored AQP4 and SLC38A1 in the LHb. Importantly, liver-specific Lcn2 overexpression recapitulated CUMS-like depressive phenotypes and LHb abnormalities, including elevated SLC22A17 and GluN2B, and largely abolished the antidepressant effects of CSS. CONCLUSION: CSS ameliorates depressive-like behaviors in association with downregulation of hepatic LCN2 and its candidate receptor SLC22A17 in the LHb, restoring ASC6-mediated glutamate homeostasis, and suppressing GluN2B-related Glutamatergic Signaling. These findings are consistent with a model in which LHb function may be modulated via the liver-brain axis through hepatic LCN2 and its candidate receptor SLC22A17, although the direct source of LHb LCN2 remains to be determined, offering experimental support for the scientific basis of CSS in "soothing the liver and relieving depression."

articles.title: Siwu Paste alleviates blood deficiency syndrome induced by cyclophosphamide and acetylphenylhydrazine in association with gut microbiota remodeling and improved splenic metabolic homeostasis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Siwu Paste (SWP), derived from the classical blood-tonifying formula Siwu Decoction, has long been used for blood deficiency-related disorders and has a well-established traditional basis and ethnopharmacological value. Blood deficiency syndrome (BDS) is a common syndrome in traditional Chinese medicine and is associated with impaired blood generation and hematopoietic dysfunction. However, the modern pharmacological mechanisms underlying the beneficial effects of SWP on BDS remain incompletely understood. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to evaluate the therapeutic effects of SWP on cyclophosphamide and acetylphenylhydrazine induced BDS and to investigate the potential mechanisms underlying its improvement of hematopoietic function. METHODS: The chemical constituents of SWP were characterized by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole-time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q-TOF-MS), and its potential mechanisms were predicted using network pharmacology. An acetylphenylhydrazine (APH)/cyclophosphamide (CTX)-induced BDS rat model was used to evaluate SWP efficacy through flow cytometry, histology, Western blotting, qPCR, 16S rRNA sequencing, and untargeted metabolomics. Broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), and exogenous adenosine diphosphate (ADP) supplementation experiments were performed to evaluate the contribution of the gut microbiota and the involvement of splenic ADP-related metabolic alterations. RESULTS: SWP significantly improved hematopoietic dysfunction, alleviated systemic inflammation, restored intestinal barrier integrity, reversed the Treg/Th17 imbalance, and reduced apoptosis within the CD45+CD34+ bone marrow cell population in BDS rats. Multi-omics analysis revealed that SWP significantly regulated gut microbiota composition and metabolic profiles; specifically, SWP treatment was associated with a significant increase in the relative abundance of Allobaculum and an upward trend in Lactobacillus, accompanied by a significant reduction in the relative abundance of total ADP in spleen tissue compared with the BDS group. FMT experiments partially transferred the hematopoietic and immunomodulatory effects associated with SWP treatment. Broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment and exogenous ADP supplementation attenuated several SWP-induced improvements in bone-marrow hematopoietic function and Treg/Th17 balance, consistent with the involvement of the gut microbiota-splenic metabolic axis in the therapeutic effects of SWP. CONCLUSION: SWP alleviates bone marrow hematopoietic dysfunction in BDS rats, with these effects accompanied by gut microbiota remodeling, restoration of intestinal barrier integrity, suppression of inflammation, and improved metabolic homeostasis. These findings provide modern pharmacological evidence supporting the traditional TCM concept of "treating the marrow via the gut" in blood deficiency-related disorders.

articles.title: Sinensetin inhibits choroidal neovascularization by downregulating the MAPK/ERK pathway.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Sinensetin (SIN), a characteristic polymethoxyflavone abundant in Citrus species, is isolated from Citrus peel (Chenpi), a medicinal material widely applied in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) to activate blood circulation and ameliorate blood stasis-associated ocular disorders. Accumulating pharmacological evidence confirms that SIN exerts prominent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-angiogenic bioactivities. It is capable of suppressing pathological angiogenesis in zebrafish and endothelial cell models, which renders SIN a promising candidate for angiogenic ocular diseases. Nevertheless, its therapeutic efficacy against choroidal neovascularization (CNV) remains largely uninvestigated. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the inhibitory effects of SIN on CNV and to dissect the underlying mechanism, specifically focusing on its modulation of FGF1-mediated MAPK/ERK signaling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The anti-CNV effect of SIN was evaluated both in vitro and in vivo. In vivo, a laser-induced CNV model was established in Brown Norway (BN) rats, and SIN was administered via intravitreal injection; CNV severity was assessed by FITC perfusion, OCT, HE staining, and Western blot. In vitro, human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) were treated with CNV-mimicking ARPE-19 human retinal pigment epithelial cells (ARPE-19) conditioned medium; the effects of SIN on migration and angiogenesis were evaluated by scratch, transwell, and tube formation assays. Combined transcriptomic and proteomic analyses were employed to screen key targets and pathways, and mechanistic validation was performed using the ERK agonist PMA and inhibitor U0126. RESULTS: In the laser-induced CNV rat model, intravitreal injection of SIN significantly reduced CNV area and thickness and suppressed the MAPK/ERK signaling pathway, effects that were reversed by the ERK agonist PMA. Consistently, in vitro experiments confirmed that SIN dose-dependently reversed the enhanced migration and tube formation of HUVEC induced by CNV-mimicking conditioned medium. Multi-omics analysis identified FGF1 as a shared candidate downstream mediator of SIN, with SIN downregulating FGF1, VEGF-A, HIF-1α, and p-ERK1/2 expression. Further mechanistic studies revealed that the ERK inhibitor U0126 mimicked the anti-angiogenic effect of SIN, whereas the ERK agonist PMA abolished its inhibitory activity, suggesting that SIN exerts anti-CNV effects, at least in part, through suppression of MAPK/ERK signaling. CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, this study demonstrates that citrus-derived SIN exerts anti-CNV effects, at least in part, through suppression of MAPK/ERK signaling, while additional pathways identified by multi-omics may also contribute. These findings highlight SIN as a promising natural product for the treatment of CNV-related ocular diseases, with FGF1 identified as a potential mediator underlying its anti-angiogenic action.

articles.title: Dihydrocaffeic acid alleviates APOE4-associated astrocyte dysfunction and cognitive impairment via LRP1/p38 MAPK signaling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Dihydrocaffeic acid (DHCA) is a phenolic acid produced through the microbial metabolism of plant-derived caffeoylquinic acids. DHCA has been detected in human plasma following oral administration of a standardized aqueous extract of Centella asiatica (L.) Urb., a medicinal plant traditionally used to improve memory and cognitive function. However, whether DHCA exerts neuroprotective effects against APOE4-associated Alzheimer's disease-like pathology remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate whether DHCA ameliorates APOE4-associated cognitive deficits and neuropathological abnormalities and to assess the role of astrocytic LRP1/p38 MAPK signaling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twelve-month-old APOE4 mice were administered DHCA once daily for 21 days, with age-matched APOE3 mice and vehicle-treated APOE4 mice serving as controls. Cognitive function, Alzheimer's disease-related neuropathology, neuronal and synaptic integrity, astrocyte phenotypes, and lipid metabolism were evaluated. Mechanistic studies were performed in APOE4-overexpressing U251 cells using siRNA-mediated LRP1 knockdown and pharmacological activation of p38 MAPK. RESULTS: DHCA improved object recognition and spatial learning and memory, reduced amyloid deposition and tau phosphorylation, restored neuronal and synaptic markers, shifted astrocyte-reactivity markers toward a neuroprotective profile, and restored proteins involved in lipid metabolism. DHCA also increased LRP1 expression and reduced p38 MAPK phosphorylation. LRP1 knockdown or p38 MAPK activation partially reversed these cellular effects. CONCLUSIONS: DHCA ameliorated APOE4-associated cognitive deficits and neuropathological alterations, at least partly through modulation of LRP1/p38 MAPK-related signaling in the APOE4-overexpressing U251 model, astrocyte reactivity, and lipid metabolism. These findings identify DHCA as a potential neuroprotective metabolite derived from plant polyphenols.

articles.title: Mechanistic insights into cholesterol-mediated MASH pathogenesis: Glycation, lipoxidation, and RAGE pathway.
articles.abstract: The pathogenesis of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is multifactorial, with evidence suggesting a pathogenic role for the AGE/ALE-RAGE axis. Although cholesterol and the AGE/ALE axis have been linked, evidence of their association in MASH remains limited. In this study, we investigated the role of the AGE/ALE-RAGE axis in cholesterol-driven MASH progression. Male C57BL/6 mice were fed either a short- or long-term high-fat, high-carbohydrate, high-cholesterol diet to induce MASH. In a subgroup of mice with MASH, the pharmacological RAGE inhibitor FPS-ZM1 (1 mg/kg/day) was administered. Mechanistic insights were further explored in vitro using HepG2 cells exposed to free fatty acids (FFAs) and oxidized LDL (oxLDL) to mimetize diet-induced MASH. Body and liver weights, adipose tissue distribution, blood glucose, liver histology, inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress, and AGE/ALE signaling were assessed. In HepG2 cells, inflammation, dicarbonyl stress, and AGE formation were evaluated. Cholesterol supplementation exacerbated MASH progression, increasing steatosis, inflammation, hepatocellular ballooning, and fibrosis, accompanied by activation of the AGE/ALE-RAGE axis, redox imbalance, and inflammation. RAGE blockade improved hepatic lipid accumulation, steatosis, inflammation, hepatocellular ballooning, AGE levels, and restored antioxidant capacity. In vitro, oxLDL induced the inflammatory response and promoted dicarbonyl stress. Collectively, these findings identify dietary cholesterol as a key modulator of MASH. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of RAGE with FPS-ZM1 effectively reversed key pathological features, supporting a functional contribution of RAGE signaling to cholesterol-associated disease severity.

articles.title: Current practices, challenges, and future directions in subcutaneous oncology monoclonal antibody delivery: a qualitative study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Subcutaneous oncology monoclonal antibodies (SCOmAbs) offer significant benefits compared to intravenous formulations, but little has been published on real-world preparation and administration practices with these products. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: This qualitative study examined 30 participants (10 patients, 10 nurses, 10 pharmacists/pharmacy technicians) across US infusion centers via in-depth interviews covering current practices, pain points, device integration potential, projected impact of increased SCOmAb adoption, and perspectives on home administration. RESULTS: Findings revealed considerable variability in SCOmAb preparation and administration practices. Notable deviations from expected workflows included bedside preparation by nurses, use of syringe pump modules, and one case of patient self-administration at home. Administration challenges included ergonomic difficulties during manual syringe injection, with nurses reporting physical discomfort and substantial workflow impact from being tethered to patients during delivery. Most patients expressed interest in home administration for time savings and flexibility, though concerns about training and safety were common. CONCLUSIONS: Though drawn from a small US sample, these hypothesis-generating findings suggest developers should consider how next-generation product presentations might minimize identified pain points and enable safe transition to home self-administration. Delivery device integration may address current challenges but requires careful consideration of facility infrastructure, workflow impact, and patient training requirements.
