articles.title: Organ-dependent phytochemical and pharmacological specialization in the endemic Adenocarpus decorticans Boiss.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Adenocarpus decorticans Boiss. is a western Mediterranean shrub restricted to Morocco and Spain, whose phytochemistry and pharmacology remain unexplored despite ethnomedicinal records reported for other species of the genus. This study reports the first organ-resolved characterisation of the species. METHODS: Hydroethanolic extracts of flowers, leaves and stems were quantified for total phenolic, flavonoid and proanthocyanidin contents and profiled by ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with electrospray ionisation mass spectrometry in targeted selected-ion monitoring mode (UHPLC-ESI-MS/SIM). Radical-scavenging and reducing reactivity was determined by DPPH, ABTS and phosphomolybdenum assays. Antibacterial activity was assessed by disc diffusion with minimum inhibitory and bactericidal concentrations against four Gram-positive and two Gram-negative strains, and antiproliferative activity against P3X63Ag8.653 murine myeloma cells and normal splenocytes by MTT. Molecular docking, 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations and ADMET profiling were performed on the identified metabolites. RESULTS: Profiling revealed pronounced organ-dependent specialization: flowers were dominated by rosmarinic acid, leaves by flavonol and flavanone glycosides, and stems by procyanidin B2 and diverse flavones. Leaves showed the highest phenolic content (526.90 mg gallic acid equivalents/g extract) and the strongest radical-scavenging reactivity (DPPH IC50 18.62 μg/mL); flowers were the most active against the Gram-positive strains, with bactericidal activity at MIC 0.78-2.08 mg/mL; and stems were the most antiproliferative against P3 cells (IC50 342.66 μg/mL) with the highest selectivity index (1.97). Docking and dynamics identified flavonoid glycosides and proanthocyanidins as the most stable binders, the EGFR-amentoflavone complex being the most stable over 100 ns. DISCUSSION: These findings reveal clear organ-driven chemical and functional specialization in A. decorticans, consistent with the traditional medicinal use documented for the species. Because all assays were performed on crude extracts, the composition-activity correspondences identify candidate constituents rather than establish their contribution, and bioassay-guided fractionation and in vivo validation remain necessary.

articles.title: Short-term superiority in proteinuria control with exploratory longitudinal trajectories: finerenone-dapagliflozin combination in non-diabetic kidney disease.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Finerenone and dapagliflozin have demonstrated renal protective effects in diabetic kidney disease, but real-world evidence on their combination in non-diabetic kidney disease (NDKD) remains scarce. We assessed whether their combination improves short-term proteinuria control versus monotherapy, with long-term trajectories explored as hypothesis-generating outcomes. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 327 NDKD patients admitted to Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital (January 2022-March 2026). Patients were divided into three groups: finerenone monotherapy, dapagliflozin monotherapy, or combination therapy. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to balance baseline characteristics. Short-term (3 months) efficacy, safety, and exploratory cost analysis were compared. Longitudinal data were analyzed using generalized estimating equations (GEE), with the primary inferential window at 3-6 months and a sensitivity analysis at 3-24 months. Multivariate logistic regression identified predictors of treatment failure in the full unmatched cohort. Exploratory subgroup analyses were performed in membranous nephropathy and hypertension. RESULTS: After PSM, at 3 months, combination therapy achieved a higher overall remission rate than dapagliflozin monotherapy (69.57% vs. 39.13%, OR = 3.56, 95% CI: 1.50-8.40, P = 0.003), but not versus finerenone monotherapy (68.29% vs. 51.22%, OR = 2.05, 95% CI: 0.84-5.05, P = 0.115). In the primary 3-6 months GEE analysis, time effects were significant for clinical remission rates and proteinuria; Sensitivity GEE analysis (3-24 months) was consistent. Descriptive analyses from 3 to 24 months showed numerical improvement trends across groups, but these are exploratory. Adverse event rates were low, but the analysis was underpowered to exclude increased hyperkalemia risk. In exploratory cost analysis, the ICER was 22.99 RMB per 1% increase in remission rate versus finerenone and 20.79 RMB versus dapagliflozin; probabilistic sensitivity analysis was broadly consistent with the base case, without judgment of economic superiority. Dapagliflozin monotherapy was independently associated with treatment failure (OR = 2.163, 95% CI: 1.073-4.362, P = 0.031) in the full unmatched cohort. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested potential benefit in membranous nephropathy and hypertension. CONCLUSION: Finerenone combined with dapagliflozin provides higher observed short-term (3 months) efficacy in NDKD, with low observed adverse event rates. Long-term outcomes require validation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomal miR-22-3p alleviates depression-like behaviors in a rat model via the FURIN/HMGB1 axis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is characterized by neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis, yet effective brain-targeted delivery strategies remain limited. Exosomes represent promising carriers capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier. This study investigated whether engineered exosomes delivering miR-22-3p by modulating the FURIN/HMGB1 axis. METHODS: Serum microRNA expression was assessed in patients with MDD. A rat model of depression was established using chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). miR-22-3p-engineered adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell exosomes were administered intranasally. Behavioral tests (SPT, OFT, FST), RT-qPCR, ELISA, HE staining, and TUNEL assays were performed to evaluate neurobehavioral and molecular changes. RESULTS: miR-22-3p was significantly downregulated in both MDD patients and CUMS rats (P < 0.01). Intranasal administration of engineered exosomes increased brain miR-22-3p levels and significantly improved depressive-like behaviors (P < 0.05 or P < 0.01). Mechanistically, treatment suppressed FURIN and HMGB1 expression, reduced proinflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α), and attenuated hippocampal neuronal apoptosis (P < 0.05 or P < 0.01). These effects were more pronounced than those of native exosomes. CONCLUSIONS: miR-22-3p-engineered exosomes exert antidepressant effects by inhibiting the FURIN/HMGB1-mediated neuroinflammatory and apoptotic pathways. This study highlights a novel intranasal exosome-based microRNA delivery strategy for MDD.

articles.title: Faricimab 6 mg versus aflibercept 8 mg in diabetic macular oedema: an in silico study of anchored efficacy and common-protocol treatment burden.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: No prospective randomised head-to-head trial has compared faricimab 6 mg with aflibercept 8 mg for diabetic macular oedema (DMO). Their pivotal programmes used materially different dosing architectures, precluding interpretation of observed interval distributions as drug properties. METHODS: We separated an anchored Bayesian aggregate-data comparison of year-1 and year-2 best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and retinal-thickness differences from an individual-level, discrete-time burden microsimulation. The latter applied identical three-dose loading and Q4W-Q16W rules, conditional on transported durability evidence. Protocol standardisation applied only to burden; dosing history did not generate efficacy. Inputs represented mixed pivotal-trial populations. Structural, prior, composite leave-out, qualification and calibration analyses were performed. RESULTS: The estimated BCVA difference between treatments was small and compatible with no treatment difference: faricimab minus aflibercept 8 mg was +1.22 letters at year 1 (95% uncertainty interval [UI], -0.48 to +2.86) and +0.41 at year 2 (-1.43 to +2.27). Retinal-thickness-reduction differences were +21.93 μm at year 1 (+1.70 to +42.52; P[Δ > 0] = 98.3%) and +20.53 μm at year 2 (-1.08 to +42.24); the year-2 interval included zero, and estimates varied across structures. Under the common simulated treat-and-extend regimen, aflibercept 8 mg was projected to require fewer injections than faricimab (7.29 vs. 8.01 by week 52 and 10.93 vs. 12.60 by week 104). A greater proportion of simulated eyes receiving aflibercept 8 mg than faricimab reached 16-week dosing intervals (80.2% vs. 50.9% at week 52 and 77.7% vs. 60.4% at week 104). Aflibercept 8 mg showed a lower estimated injection burden, although the adjusted range included no difference between treatments. CONCLUSION: The estimated BCVA differences were small and compatible with no treatment difference. Faricimab showed greater anatomical improvement at year 1, while the year-2 estimate included no difference. Aflibercept 8 mg showed a lower simulated injection burden, although the adjusted range included no difference. Neither treatment demonstrated clinical superiority.

articles.title: Alda-1 reduces chronic and post-deprivation nicotine intake in rats: impact of concurrent ethanol consumption on treatment efficacy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nicotine dependence is characterized by high relapse rates, often complicated by comorbid alcohol consumption. Both substances dysregulate glutamatergic signaling and promote oxidative stress in the nucleus accumbens (NAc), mechanisms that may contribute to persistent drug seeking. This study evaluated the therapeutic potential of Alda-1, an activator of mitochondrial aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2), to reduce nicotine and concurrent ethanol/nicotine intake, post-deprivation reaccess, and examined its association with accumbal glutamate homeostasis. METHODS: Female alcohol-preferring UChB rats were induced to voluntarily consume nicotine or a combination of nicotine and ethanol. Rats received Alda-1 (25 mg/kg, p. o.) or vehicle during chronic maintenance and during a 14-day deprivation period. Extracellular glutamate levels in NAc were assessed by, and GLT-1 levels were determined by Western blot. RESULTS: Alda-1 administration significantly suppressed chronic nicotine intake by 67% and reduced post-deprivation nicotine consumption by 82%. These behavioral changes were accompanied by a 40% reduction in extracellular glutamate levels in the NAc, restoring them to baseline levels observed in naïve controls. In the co-consumption model, Alda-1 effectively reduced chronic ethanol and nicotine intake by 80%-90%. However, Alda-1 failed to reduce post-deprivation intake in the dual-substance paradigm. This lack of efficacy was accompanied by GLT-1 downregulation induced by concurrent ethanol/nicotine exposure, which was not reversed by Alda-1. CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate that ALDH2 activation by Alda-1 markedly reduced chronic and post-deprivation nicotine intake, an effect associated with improved glutamate homeostasis. Alda-1 also attenuates chronic polysubstance use; however, its efficacy is lost during post-deprivation re-access in the co-consumption model associated with GLT-1 downregulation, suggesting synergistic neuroadaptations may bypass ALDH2-mediated pathways.

articles.title: Potentially harmful excipients in drugs: an analysis of labeling practices and adverse drug reactions.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Excipients play a crucial role in pharmaceutical formulations, however, their safety profile in pediatric populations remains inadequately characterized. METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study was conducted in two phases. Phase one reviewed package inserts of pediatric medications used at seven Fujian hospitals (July 2019-June 2024) to assess excipient labeling. Phase two analyzed associations between potentially harmful excipients (PHEs) exposure and adverse drug reactions using the reporting odds ratio (ROR) method at a single children's hospital. RESULTS: The rates of excipient labeling exhibited significant variation based on hospital type, drug source, and drug category. In total, 41.3% of pediatric cases and 43.2% of prescriptions included at least one PHE. Benzyl alcohol was associated with application site pain (ROR = 393.20, P < 0.05) and erythema (ROR = 85.84, P < 0.05); thimerosal was linked to application site irritation (ROR = 278.35, P < 0.05) and pruritus (ROR = 115.20, P < 0.05); and sodium citrate was associated with bradycardia (ROR = 157.59, P < 0.05). CONCLUSION: The labeling of excipients in pediatric pharmaceutical products is insufficient in the institutions examined, potentially hindering the identification of excipient exposure in clinical practice. The safety signals identified in this study necessitate further systematic investigation and careful consideration within both regulatory and clinical contexts.

articles.title: Scorpion toxin peptide BMK86-P1 achieves mutation-reversible inhibition of KCNA2 at the cost of reduced efficacy in heteromers and murine neurons.
articles.abstract: The discovery of distinctive function-phenotype relationships in monogenetic channelopathies has turned out to be critical for the development of precision medicine approaches. However, the most accurate prediction of clinical phenotypes depends on neuronal function, where existing models lack tools to isolate currents of individual voltage-gated potassium channel subunits and to differentiate variant effects in complex systems. Ideally, one should be able to overexpress subunit variants with an additional mutation that would confer resistance against the tool used to isolate the variant effect. Therefore, we solid-phase synthesized the KV1.2 specific scorpion toxin peptide BMK86-P1 and oxidized it with modest efficacy. In mammalian cells this BMK86-P1 selectively inhibited KV1.2 homomers, but not heteromers with KV1.1. Critically, the KCNA2 p. Val381Tyr mutation, which reverses BMK86-P1's selective inhibition of KV1.2, also altered the activation of KV1.2 homomers to resemble those of KV1.1. In addition, in murine neurons, BMK86-P1 did not alter passive membrane properties, single action potential properties, or action potential firing. Surprisingly, it induced only minimal changes in spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic currents. In summary, this KV1.2 subunit selective toxin peptide primarily affects homomeric channels, while only weakly inhibiting KV1.2/KV1.1 heteromeric channels and consequently preventing any meaningful impact on neuronal function. This highlights the limitations of peptide synthesis together with the need for testing specific compounds on complex systems.

articles.title: A redox-inflammasome threshold model of ovulation: a hypothesis on NLRP3-Mediated regulation.
articles.abstract: Ovulation is a highly coordinated biological process involving endocrine regulation, tissue remodeling, immune activation, metabolic adaptation, and redox signaling. Although inflammatory responses are recognized as essential components of follicular rupture, the mechanisms integrating oxidative stress, metabolic alterations, and inflammasome activation during ovulatory progression remain incompletely understood. Here, we propose a hypothesis-driven redox-inflammasome threshold model of ovulatory regulation, in which NLRP3 inflammasome signaling may serve as an important integrator of redox and metabolic cues that modulate inflammatory remodeling during the periovulatory period. This model suggests that successful ovulation requires a precisely balanced inflammatory threshold, whereas insufficient or excessive inflammasome activation may disrupt follicular homeostasis and contribute to ovarian dysfunction. Importantly, NLRP3 is proposed not as an indispensable determinant of follicular rupture, but as one regulatory component within a complex network involving cytokines, prostaglandins, matrix metalloproteinases, immune cells, and hormonal signals. By integrating current evidence linking mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, metabolic stress, and inflammation, this hypothesis provides a conceptual framework for understanding ovulation as a redox-sensitive immune-metabolic process. Future studies using cell type-specific NLRP3 manipulation, quantitative redox analysis, and single-cell approaches will be required to determine the physiological contribution of inflammasome signaling to ovulatory regulation.

articles.title: Evaluating student perceptions of image-based audience response questions in medical education.
articles.abstract: Audience response systems have been extensively utilized in medical and pharmacy education to improve learner engagement and knowledge retention. Unlike traditional ARSs that utilize text-based multiple-choice questions Hotspot is an image-based ARS integrated into PointSolutions that allows students to answer questions by selecting areas of interest on images and figures, rather than choosing from multiple-choice options. The purpose of this study was to evaluate student perceptions of integrating Hotspot into pharmacology and biomedical curricula, including perceived engagement, learning reinforcement, usability and preferences relative to traditional MCQs. Faculty at California Northstate University incorporated Hotspot questions into the lectures of first- and second-year courses across three matriculating classes. Following these sessions, students completed an anonymous survey. Survey items assessed student perceptions of engagement, perceived learning, and ease of use on a seven-point Likert scale. Learners reported that Hotspot technology made it easier to pay attention during lectures (median Likert score of six out of seven [interquartile range (IQR) 5-7]; n = 99). They felt the questions were a good use of class time (6 out of 7 [interquartile range 6-7]; n = 99) and indicated that the interactive format challenged them and reinforced their understanding better than MCQs (6 out of 7 [IQR 5-7]; n = 99). Overall, learners expressed a preference for Hotspot over traditional MCQs and reported that this approach was more engaging. These findings support the feasibility and learner acceptability of incorporating image-based active learning strategies and provide evidence to support the adoption of innovative instructional approaches in medical and pharmacology education.

articles.title: Irrigation fluid absorption induces metabolic and oxidative stress dysregulation activating NLRP3 and NF-κB pathways to drive hippocampal inflammatory responses.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Irrigation fluid absorption during endoscopic procedures can lead to serious complications, but its effects on hippocampal function remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the impact of irrigation fluid absorption on hippocampal metabolic homeostasis and inflammatory responses. METHODS: Adult female Sprague-Dawley rats received intravenous 0.9% saline (control, 40 mL/kg, or 80 mL/kg) to simulate irrigation fluid absorption. Saline was infused over 30 min, and the animals were euthanized 15 min after cessation of anesthesia, corresponding to 45 min after initiation of the infusion. We assessed emergence time from anesthesia, hippocampal energy metabolism through targeted metabolomics, mitochondrial ultrastructure via transmission electron microscopy (TEM), oxidative stress markers, and NLRP3- and NF-κB-related inflammatory markers. RESULTS: The 80 mL/kg group showed significantly prolonged anesthesia emergence time compared to controls (59.0 ± 13.5 vs. 31.7 ± 4.5 s; p < 0.01). Metabolomics revealed dose-dependent perturbations in the TCA cycle, glycolysis, and oxidative phosphorylation (p < 0.05). TEM analysis demonstrated severe mitochondrial ultrastructural damage in hippocampal neurons, including dose-dependent swelling, internal membrane disruption, and matrix dissolution. Both absorption groups showed altered glutathione redox status, characterized by increased GSSG levels and decreased GSH/GSSG ratios (p < 0.01), whereas SOD, CAT, MDA, NADPH, and GSH exhibited heterogeneous and non-linear changes across doses. At this early endpoint, increased NLRP3, P50/P65, IL-6, IL-18, and IL-33 immunoreactivity, together with decreased IκB immunoreactivity, indicated early changes in NLRP3- and NF-κB-related inflammatory signaling. CONCLUSION: Excessive irrigation fluid absorption induces hippocampal neuroinflammation through metabolic disturbance and redox dysregulation, which activates NLRP3 and NF-κB pathways. These findings suggest potential therapeutic targets for preventing neurological complications during endoscopic procedures.

articles.title: Conditional approval of oncology medicines in Europe (2017-2022): evidence maturity, regulatory outcomes, clinical benefit and downstream access.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Conditional marketing authorisation (CMA) is a European regulatory pathway that enables earlier access to medicines for serious conditions while allowing additional evidence generation after approval. Important questions remain regarding the maturity of supporting evidence, subsequent regulatory outcomes, clinical benefit, and patient access. We characterised the evidentiary basis, regulatory outcomes, clinical benefit, clinical practice guideline incorporation, and downstream access of oncology medicines granted CMA between 2017 and 2022. METHODS: We analysed all antineoplastic medicines granted CMA by the European Commission between 1 January 2017 and 31 December 2022. European Medicines Agency documentation was reviewed to assess regulatory characteristics, post-authorisation obligations, pivotal studies, and outcomes through 31 March 2025. Clinical benefit was evaluated using ESMO-MCBS, while reimbursement was assessed in Spain as an illustrative case of downstream access as of 15 December 2025. Kaplan-Meier analysis estimated time to regulatory resolution and reimbursement. RESULTS: Twenty-six antineoplastic medicines received CMA, representing 55.3% of all CMA approvals. Most pivotal studies were single-arm (92.9%), open-label, and used surrogate primary endpoints, with a median efficacy sample size of 100.5 participants (IQR 78.5-128.0). Thirty-five specific obligations were imposed, with a median time of 3.95 years (IQR 1.73-5.23) from CMA approval to the latest due date. By 31 March 2025, 53.8% remained under CMA, 38.5% converted to standard marketing authorisation, and 7.7% were withdrawn. Median time to regulatory resolution was 4.46 years. Only 16.7% (3/18) demonstrated substantial clinical benefit according to ESMO-MCBS. Most medicines were subsequently incorporated into ESMO or EHA clinical practice guidelines, although only five (19.2%) received an IA recommendation corresponding to their first CMA-approved indication; two additional medicines received IA recommendations in earlier treatment settings. Public reimbursement was granted for 84.6% (22/26), with a median time of 2.38 years. CONCLUSION: Oncology medicines granted CMA were frequently supported by limited and immature evidence, while substantial clinical benefit was uncommon and regulatory resolution often required several years. Future optimisation should combine timely access with timely post-authorisation evidence generation, including comparative clinical and real-world evidence.

articles.title: N-acetylcysteine ameliorates oxidative stress-induced decline in sex hormone-binding globulin in HepG2 cells and polycystic ovary syndrome rats.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Low sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) levels are a significant indicator of hyperandrogenism severity in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and are associated with an increased risk of reproductive and metabolic diseases. Oxidative stress suppresses the production and secretion of SHBG. However, the effect of the antioxidant N-acetylcysteine (NAC) on hepatic SHBG expression remains unknown. This study investigated the effects of NAC on SHBG expression and the underlying mechanism in HepG2 cells and a rat model of PCOS. METHODS: HepG2 cells were treated with testosterone propionate (TP), oxidized high-density lipoprotein (ox-HDL), oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL), and NAC. Female Sprague-Dawley rats aged 28 days were randomly allocated to eight groups: control, PCOS, and control and PCOS groups treated with NAC at 100, 200, or 400 mg/kg body weight. The PCOS rat model, induced by TP and a high-fat, high-sugar diet, was treated with different doses of NAC for 8 weeks. The expression of SHBG, hepatocyte nuclear factor 4α (HNF4α), chicken ovalbumin upstream promoter-transcription factor 1 (COUP-TF1), and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ (PPAR-γ) was assessed in HepG2 cells and rat liver tissue. Metabolic, hormonal, and oxidative stress indices were analyzed in the rat model. RESULTS: In HepG2 cells, TP and oxidized lipoprotein treatments significantly suppressed SHBG and HNF4α expression, while NAC treatment reversed the inhibitory effects induced by ox-HDL and ox-LDL (P < 0.05). In PCOS rats, NAC intervention increased the mRNA and protein levels of SHBG by upregulating HNF4α and downregulating COUP-TF1 and PPAR-γ expression in the liver; increased serum SHBG; reduced hepatocytic reactive oxygen species levels (P < 0.05); and ameliorated obesity, estrous cycle abnormalities, hepatic steatosis, circulating sex hormone levels, and the lipid profile, with 200 mg/kg NAC showing the most favorable overall pattern among the three doses tested. CONCLUSION: NAC treatment ameliorates oxidative stress-induced decreases in SHBG and HNF4α expression in HepG2 cells and may restore hepatocytic SHBG production by upregulating HNF4α and downregulating COUP-TF1/PPAR-γ expression in rats with PCOS.

articles.title: Economic evaluation of six immune checkpoint inhibitor-based first-line therapies for advanced squamous non-small-cell lung cancer: a cost-effectiveness analysis based on network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Advanced squamous non-small-cell lung cancer (sq-NSCLC) imposes a substantial clinical and economic burden. Immune checkpoint inhibitors (sugemalimab, tislelizumab, penpulimab, serplulimab, camrelizumab, and pembrolizumab) combined with chemotherapy improve survival, but their comparative cost-effectiveness remains uncertain. METHODS: A three-state partitioned survival model with 3-week cycles and a lifetime horizon was developed from the Chinese healthcare-system perspective. Clinical efficacy was derived from six phase 3 trials and synthesized using network meta-analysis. Costs, life-years (LYs), quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) for each ICI-based regimen versus chemotherapy were estimated. The willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold was set at $27,906/QALY. Deterministic, probabilistic, scenario, and full incremental analyses were performed. RESULTS: In the base-case analysis, chemotherapy alone yielded 0.71 QALYs at $12,227.47. All ICI-based regimens increased QALYs to between 1.24 and 2.07. Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy provided the greatest health benefit, yielding 2.07 QALYs, but had an ICER of $70,913.04 per QALY versus chemotherapy alone. Penpulimab plus chemotherapy had the lowest ICER versus chemotherapy alone ($13,064.23 per QALY), followed by camrelizumab ($13,361.50/QALY), and tislelizumab plus chemotherapy ($14,022.95/QALY), all below the WTP threshold. Sugemalimab plus chemotherapy and serplulimab plus chemotherapy exceeded the threshold. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis indicated that camrelizumab plus chemotherapy had the highest probability of being cost-effective (95%) at $27,906/QALY. In the full incremental analysis, the efficiency frontier comprised chemotherapy alone, penpulimab plus chemotherapy, camrelizumab plus chemotherapy, and pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy; camrelizumab plus chemotherapy was the preferred strategy after dominated options were excluded. CONCLUSION: At the selected WTP threshold, camrelizumab plus chemotherapy may be the preferred first-line strategy after strictly and extendedly dominated alternatives were excluded. This finding depends on the indirect comparisons, chemotherapy baseline, drug prices, survival extrapolation, and post-progression assumptions.

articles.title: Repurposing farnesyltransferase inhibitors tipifarnib and lonafarnib as antibacterial agents: proteomic and functional analyses.
articles.abstract: Farnesyltransferase inhibitors (FTIs) like tipifarnib and lonafarnib, originally developed as anticancer agents, show antibacterial activity against Gram-positive pathogens through an unknown mechanism of action. Here, we investigated the proteomic response of Bacillus subtilis 168 (Gram-positive) and an efflux-deficient Escherichia coli ΔtolC mutant (Gram-negative) to sublethal concentrations of FTIs. Concentrations resulting in approximately 50% growth inhibition were applied, followed by two complementary proteomic approaches: gel-free quantitative LC-HDMSE (both organisms) and 2D-PAGE with [35S]-methionine pulse labelling of newly synthesized proteins (B. subtilis). Marker proteins from the B. subtilis 2D-PAGE approach were used for comparative proteomic response profiling against a reference library of 96 antibacterial agents. Bacillus subtilis was more susceptible to both FTIs than E. coli ΔtolC, with tipifarnib being more potent. LC-HDMSE analysis revealed a pronounced cell envelope stress signature in B. subtilis, including regulation of YocH, YabE, and YjhA, along with several σB, σW, and σM-regulated stress proteins. In the 2D-PAGE analysis, reflecting acute cellular responses by monitoring newly synthesized proteins, both FTIs induced proteins such as ClpC, PspA, and LiaH. Comparative proteomic response analysis in B. subtilis showed that both FTIs cluster with membrane-active antibiotics, including xanthoangelol, MP196, gramicidin S, MP66, and nisin, which binds the cell wall precursor lipid II and forms pores in the bacterial membrane. Similarities were also observed with pseudopterosin G and pseudopteroxazole, which target the bacterial cell envelope by integration into the membrane and interfering with membrane-bound steps of cell wall biosynthesis. Yet, the similarity of the proteomic profiles does not indicate a perfect match or an identical molecular mode of action within the reference library. In E. coli ΔtolC, the proteomic response was less pronounced, but for treatment with tipifarnib, regulated proteins of the category "membrane-bounded periplasmic space" were enriched. Proteomic profiling, combined with functional validation via membrane integrity and membrane potential assays, indicates that FTIs compromise the bacterial membrane and activate stress and repair pathways. The FTIs may also indirectly affect cell wall biosynthesis. The lack of a perfect match with any of the 96 compounds in the proteomic reference library highlights FTIs as promising lead structures for the development of novel antibiotics.

articles.title: Synergistic induction of apoptosis in human prostate cancer PC3 cells by silver-coated cerium oxide nanoparticles: unveiling the role of ROS-mediated p53-associated apoptotic signaling and antioxidant system depletion.
articles.abstract: Castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) represents a formidable clinical challenge due to intrinsic defects in apoptotic execution, elevated baseline antioxidant capacity, and rapid resistance to standard chemotherapy. Herein, we report the rational design, template-directed synthesis, and antineoplastic evaluation of silver-coated cerium oxide core-shell nanoparticles (Ag@CeO2 NPs) derived from a cerium-based metal-organic framework (Ce-UiO-66) for targeted intervention in androgen-independent prostate carcinoma. Uniform Ce-UiO-66 MOF nanoparticles were thermally converted via controlled calcination (550 °C, 3 h) into porous cubic fluorite nanoceria (CeO₂) cores, followed by in situ surface nucleation and reduction of a metallic silver (Ag⁰) nanoshell stabilized by polyvinylpyrrolidone. The physicochemical properties were characterized by FTIR, PXRD, FESEM, EDX mapping, DLS, and Zeta potential analysis. In vitro anticancer efficacy was evaluated in human androgen-independent PC-3 prostate cancer cells and normal human fibroblasts (HFF-1). Cellular viability, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT) enzymatic kinetics, apoptosis-related transcriptomics (p53, Bax, Bcl-2 via qRT-PCR), and p53 protein levels (ELISA) were systematically quantified. PXRD and Scherrer analysis confirmed the formation of pure, face-centered cubic fluorite CeO₂ (Cerianite-(Ce), Fm3̄m, *a* = 5.4110 Å) with an average primary crystallite size of 7.27 ± 0.36 nm (7.44 nm for the (111) reflection), alongside characteristic reflections of metallic Ag. FESEM, DLS, and electrophoretic measurements revealed spherical, cauliflower-like hierarchical clusters with a hydrodynamic diameter (Z-average) of 111.68 nm, narrow polydispersity (PDI = 0.2860), and stable negative surface charge (ζ = - 14.96 mV). The Ag@CeO2 NPs displayed pronounced, tumor-selective cytotoxicity, yielding an IC₅₀ of 32.14 µg/mL against PC-3 cells while sparing normal HFF-1 fibroblasts (IC₅₀ = 171.6 µg/mL, > 5.3-fold selectivity window). Mechanistically, the nanocomposite triggered a severe, concentration-dependent intracellular ROS burst (*p* < 0.0001 at 30 µM) accompanied by the functional collapse of the cellular antioxidant barrier through profound suppression of SOD (*p* < 0.01) and CAT (*p* < 0.0001) activities. This unmitigated oxidative crisis was associated with increased TP53 transcript levels and increased p53-associated protein signals as measured by ELISA (*p* < 0.0001), which coincided with upregulated Bax, downregulated Bcl-2, and elevated the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio (*p* < 0.001), consistent with activation of mitochondrial apoptotic signaling. Ag@CeO2 NPs function as a potent, tumor-selective pro-oxidant nanotherapeutic platform capable of overriding endogenous antioxidant defenses, enhancing p53-associated apoptotic signaling and promoting mitochondrial apoptotic responses, suggesting that Ag@CeO2 NPs may serve as a potential candidate for further investigation in prostate cancer nanomedicine.

articles.title: The gut microbiota-IPA axis mediated by catalpol alleviates DSS-induced colitis through AhR activation.
articles.abstract: Current management strategies for colitis predominantly involve broad immunosuppression, underscoring the urgent need for strategies that restore essential homeostatic pathways. Insufficient activation of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) by microbial metabolites compromises its crucial role in maintaining mucosal integrity, a defect commonly observed in colitis. While the natural compound catalpol exhibits preventive potential, its precise function within host-microbiota crosstalk remained undefined. This study aims to investigate the protective effects of catalpol on colitis, focusing on the role of gut microbiota and its metabolite, indole-3-propionic acid (IPA). A mouse model of DSS-induced colitis was utilized. The protective outcomes and mechanisms were assessed through integrated multi-omics analyses, functional validation via microbial manipulation, and molecular studies confirming the activation of the AhR pathway. In this study, catalpol protects against DSS-induced colitis in mice, and this protection is associated with alterations in gut microbiota composition. Integrated multi-omics analysis suggests that catalpol treatment is associated with increased relative abundance of Lachnospiraceae at the family level and with elevated levels of the microbial metabolite indole-3-propionic acid. Functional validation through fecal microbiota transplantation from catalpol-treated mice or direct IPA supplementation partially reproduced several protective effects, suggesting that IPA may be a downstream mediator contributing to the protective effects of catalpol. Molecular analyses indicate that both catalpol and IPA can physically interact with AhR. Importantly, pharmacological suppression of AhR partially reversed the protective effects, suggesting that AhR activation contributes to the protective effects of catalpol. Collectively, these findings suggest that catalpol protects against DSS-induced colitis, and this effect is associated with increased relative abundance of Lachnospiraceae at the family level and elevated IPA levels, potentially contributing to a microbiota-IPA-AhR axis. This work highlights the preventive potential of restoring host-microbiota metabolic crosstalk and provides a rationale for developing microbiota-targeted protective strategies.

articles.title: Contraindication-adjusted prescription omission patterns of RASi, beta-blockers, and MRAs in hospitalized heart failure: associations with 30-day and 1-year mortality.
articles.abstract: Guideline directed therapy is still underused in heart failure and little is known about how missing specific medications near discharge relates to survival. The aim of this study is to examine whether study-defined omission patterns of RASi (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or ARNIs), beta-blockers, and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) in the final 48 h before discharge were associated with short-term and 1-year mortality among hospitalized adults with heart failure. Adult admissions with a recorded heart failure diagnosis were identified using ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes. The three classes were RASi, beta-blockers, and MRAs (SGLT2 inhibitors were not included). A contraindication-adjusted operational framework was used to identify admissions without selected laboratory or hemodynamic barriers to these therapies and to classify late-hospital prescription omission patterns. Final-48-h orders were a proxy for treatment near discharge, not a reconciled discharge list. This framework did not establish heart failure phenotype-specific guideline eligibility. Associations with mortality within 30 and 365 days after discharge were evaluated using multivariable regression models. The final analytic cohort included 57,098 admissions from 24,922 patients. The reference group with prescriptions for all three study classes was small whereas omission of 2 or 3 therapies was substantially more common across the cohort. Admissions with prescriptions for all three study classes had the lowest 365-day mortality (13.88%). Crude 365-day mortality was higher in all omission groups, reaching 30.84% when RASi and beta-blocker were omitted and 27.50% when all three classes were omitted. In adjusted analyses, omission of all 3 therapies was associated with higher 30-day mortality (OR = 1.67). For 365-day mortality, the strongest adverse association was observed for omission of renin-angiotensin system inhibitor plus beta-blocker (HR = 1.33). Late-hospital omission patterns involving RASi and omission of all three study therapies were associated with higher post-discharge mortality. As heart failure phenotype and left-ventricular ejection fraction were not incorporated into the eligibility definition, these findings should be interpreted as prognostic associations of prescribing patterns rather than causal effects of withholding guideline-indicated HFrEF therapy.

articles.title: Combined melatonin and edaravone therapy attenuates methylmercury-induced amyotrophic lateral sclerosis-like neurodegeneration through GLP-1 modulation and myelin preservation.
articles.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive and fatal neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the selective degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons, resulting in progressive muscle weakness, paralysis, and respiratory failure. Despite the availability of disease-modifying therapies, current treatment options provide only modest clinical benefits, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic strategies targeting multiple pathological mechanisms. Melatonin, a pleiotropic neuroprotective molecule with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic properties, has emerged as a promising candidate; however, its influence on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-associated neuroprotective signaling and related molecular events in ALS remains poorly understood. Therefore, the present study investigated the neuroprotective efficacy of melatonin in a methylmercury (MTMR)-induced rat model of ALS and explored its effects on GLP-1-associated molecular alterations, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, neurotransmitter homeostasis, demyelination, and neuronal injury. Molecular docking analysis was performed to predict the interaction of melatonin with proteins implicated in ALS pathology. Adult Wistar rats were exposed to MTMR (5 mg/kg, p.o.) for 21 days to induce ALS-like neurodegeneration, followed by treatment with melatonin (5 or 10 mg/kg, i.p.), edaravone (3 mg/kg, i.p.), or their combination for an additional 21 days. Neurobehavioral performance, biochemical alterations, hematological parameters, molecular biomarkers, and histopathological changes were subsequently evaluated. MTMR administration produced profound motor deficits accompanied by reduced GLP-1 levels, neurotransmitter imbalance, increased neuroinflammatory and apoptotic markers, elevated neurofilament light chain (NEFL), skeletal muscle injury, methylmercury accumulation, and extensive myelin and neuronal damage. Melatonin treatment significantly attenuated these pathological alterations in a dose-dependent manner by increasing GLP-1 levels, improving antioxidant status, reducing inflammatory and apoptotic responses, restoring neurotransmitter balance, preserving myelin integrity, and improving neuronal morphology across multiple brain regions and the spinal cord. Molecular docking further predicted favorable interactions between melatonin and several proteins associated with ALS pathophysiology, supporting its potential as a multitarget therapeutic agent. In most outcome measures, combined treatment with melatonin and edaravone produced greater neuroprotective effects than either intervention alone. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that melatonin substantially attenuates methylmercury-induced ALS-like neuropathology through coordinated modulation of multiple pathological processes associated with neurodegeneration. Although the precise molecular mechanisms require further experimental validation, the observed restoration of GLP-1 levels together with improvements in oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, apoptosis, neurotransmitter homeostasis, and myelin integrity suggests that melatonin may represent a promising adjunctive therapeutic strategy for ALS.

articles.title: Hesperetin-loaded transethosomes for management of skin cancer: formulation and optimization by Box-Behnken design and in vitro, ex vivo, and dermatokinetic studies.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop and optimize hesperetin-loaded transethosomes (HSP-TEs) to ameliorate skin cancer, yet enhancing skin permeability, deposition, and stability. HSP-TEs were prepared using thin-film hydration and optimized through a Box-Behnken design (BBD). The optimized formulation exhibited a vesicle size of 134.27 ± 3.17 nm, polydispersity index of 0.209 ± 0.006, zeta potential of - 27.39 ± 0.53 mV, and entrapment efficiency of 90.33 ± 3.88%, confirming nanoscale stability and uniformity. HSP-TEs were further incorporated into a Carbopol-based HSP-TE loaded gel (HSP-TEG) for topical application. Comparative in vitro release studies revealed sustained release from HSP-TEs (71.77 ± 6.79%), followed by HSP-TEG (60.03 ± 4.13%) at 24 h, whereas significantly lower release was observed from hesperetin suspension (HSP-S, 32.23 ± 5.09%) and hesperetin-suspension gel (HSP-SG, 25.76 ± 3.55%) at 24 h. Ex vivo permeation studies demonstrated superior skin penetration from HSP-TEs (63.70 ± 5.19%) and HSP-TEG (51.03 ± 3.12%) compared to HSP-S (27.23 ± 2.16%) and HSP-SG (23.87 ± 1.09%) at 24 h. Confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) analysis of HSP-TEs revealed greater skin permeability. Dermatokinetic analysis confirmed enhanced epidermal and dermal drug deposition from HSP-TEG. The cytotoxicity studies in A431 epidermoid carcinoma cells demonstrated greater time- and concentration-dependent anticancer effects for HSP-TEs relative to free drug (p < 0.05). The optimized formulation revealed sustained release and improved permeability and stability, suggesting a promising platform for management skin cancer.

articles.title: Tislelizumab-induced immune-mediated hepatotoxicity combined with two episodes of hepatitis B virus reactivation: a case report.
articles.abstract: Immune-mediated hepatotoxicity (IMH) is a typical immune-related adverse event associated with the use of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), while hepatitis B virus reactivation (HBVr) is an infectious complication that may also occur during ICI therapy. However, these two conditions are usually independent and rarely co-occur in the same individual. Herein, we describe a patient with lung squamous cell carcinoma who developed HBVr and IMH simultaneously after receiving tislelizumab, and the co-existence of two episodes of HBVr brings challenges to the diagnosis and treatment of IMH. In the diagnosis of IMH, the co-existence of HBVr masked the underlying IMH, resulting in a delay in IMH treatment. In the treatment of IMH, the re-occurrence of HBVr led to a dilemma of continuing to use glucocorticoids (GCs) or stopping them. In such a clinical scenario, the multidisciplinary approach, close monitoring of liver function and HBV-DNA, and a carefully balanced treatment strategy combining GCs with intensified antiviral therapy are essential to realize the optimal management for IMH. In conclusion, medical staff should be alert to the coexistence of HBVr and IMH in patients receiving ICIs, so as to avoid missed diagnosis and treatment delay.

articles.title: Next-Generation Bioinspired Microneedle Systems for Peptide Delivery: Bridging Design and Translational Medicine.
articles.abstract: Peptide-based therapies have transformed the management of chronic illnesses such as diabetes, cancer, and cardiovascular problems, owing to their remarkable specificity, effectiveness, and low toxicity. Nonetheless, their therapeutic efficacy is frequently impeded by obstacles such as inadequate bioavailability, fast enzymatic breakdown, and restricted systemic stability. Conventional delivery strategies, such as oral and intravenous injection, have considerable constraints in efficiently transporting peptides to target locations. Transdermal drug delivery systems, especially microneedles (MNs) and bioinspired microneedles (BMNs), have garnered considerable interest as a less invasive and effective option to surmount these obstacles. MNs form microchannels in the epidermis and dermis, facilitating the direct administration of peptides into systemic circulation, hence dramatically improving peptide delivery across the skin. Recent improvements in BMNs technology have enhanced peptide delivery through better mechanical strength, skin contact, and controlled release. This paper mainly focuses on the importance of peptide drugs, the obstacles related to their administration, and the potential of BMNs for effective transdermal delivery. We emphasize current advancements in BMNs that improve peptide stability, permeability, and therapeutic effectiveness, facilitating their practical use in the treatment of chronic and acute disorders.

articles.title: A single exposure to the environmental contaminant tributyltin induces oxidative stress and vascular endothelial dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Organotin compounds, such as tributyltin (TBT), are environmental contaminants known for toxic effects. Subacute exposure to TBT leads to vascular dysfunction associated with increased production of reactive oxygen species (ROS). This study aimed to investigate whether a single exposure to TBT induces endothelial dysfunction. Adult female rats were divided into two groups: control (CT) and TBT-exposed. Vascular reactivity of isolated aortic rings was assessed 24hours after a single oral dose of TBT (500ng/kg). Vasodilator responses to acetylcholine and sodium nitroprusside were not altered by TBT exposure. However, aortic rings from TBT-exposed rats exhibited greater contractile response to phenylephrine and reduced influence of endothelial denudation or L-NAME incubation on vascular reactivity. The impaired nitrergic modulation induced by TBT was prevented by co-incubation with superoxide dismutase plus L-NAME. In vitro DAF-2 assay indicated reduced NO production in the TBT group. TBT-induced vascular hyperreactivity was reversed by incubation with apocynin, TIRON, catalase, allopurinol, losartan, indomethacin, NS-398, SQ-29,548, and SC-19,220. In contrast, the non-selective NOX inhibitor VAS2870 did not modify the response to phenylephrine. Dihydroethidium staining showed increased ROS levels- including superoxide anion and hydrogen peroxide-in aortas from TBT-exposed animals. Scanning electron microscopy revealed endothelial structural damage in the TBT group. Together, these findings indicate that a single dose of TBT (500ng/kg) caused vascular dysfunction, likely resulting from impaired endothelial and nitrergic modulation mediated by increased ROS production derived from xanthine oxidase, activation of the local renin-angiotensin system, and cyclooxygenase pathways in female rats.

articles.title: Proposal for a revised TSCA carbon tetrachloride existing chemical exposure limit (ECEL) based on PBPK and benchmark dose modeling.
articles.abstract: Carbon tetrachloride (CTC) is classified by the United States Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA) as "likely to be carcinogenic to humans," based on evidence in mice. In 2021, under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA), US EPA derived a CTC cancer existing chemical exposure limit (ECEL) of 0.03 parts per million (ppm) for occupational exposure, and in 2024, released its Final Risk Management Rule incorporating this ECEL. However, US EPA's CTC ECEL is considerably lower than global occupational exposure limits (OELs) (0.1-10 ppm), and arguably not consistent with the best available science, as mandated by TSCA. In its derivation of the liver cancer ECEL, US EPA applied the lowest observed adverse effect concentration (LOAEC)/no observed adverse effect concentration (NOAEC) approach, rather than benchmark dose (BMD) modeling, and did not use CTC-specific physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models for animal-to-human extrapolation. Here we derive revised cancer and non-cancer CTC ECELs of 1.5 and 1.6 ppm, respectively, considering the most reliable and sensitive endpoints and scientifically supported methodologies, including BMD and PBPK modeling. The revised cancer ECEL is 50-fold higher than US EPA's ECEL, more consistent with global OELs, and well below the OSHA permissible exposure limit (PEL) of 10 ppm. Overall, this approach would be expected to be applicable to other chemicals with a similar mode of action.

articles.title: NanoMiLens (Nano-Micelle Loaded Hydrogel Contact Lenses) of Tofacitinib Citrate: Amalgamation, Development, Optimization and Characterization.
articles.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a multifactorial inflammatory eye disease caused mainly by immune dysregulation through JAK/STAT, which leads to a turbulent tear film, damage to the corneal epithelia, and poor visualization. Topical therapies of the conventional type show less ocular bioavailability with quick precorneal excretion. This research was done to design and test a new NanoMiLens system loaded with Tofacitinib Citrate (TFC), which is a selective JAK inhibitor, in order to have a controlled and prolonged contact lens delivery manageable with DED. TFC Polymeric Nano-Micelles (PoT-PNMs) were prepared using a thin-film hydration method employing Poloxamer 407 as the amphiphilic polymer and Tween 80 as the stabilizing surfactant in acetone, then rehydrated with simulated tear fluid. PBD ANOVA confirmed polymer concentration and surfactant concentration as dominant factors for EE%. CCD quadratic modelling yielded R2 = 0.9904 for EE%, 0.9789 for CDR%, and 0.9408 for particle size, with model validation errors < 1%. The optimized PoT-PNMs (200 mg Poloxamer 407, 0.30 mL Tween 80) achieved particle size 92 ± 2.6 nm, PDI 0.246, EE% 90.60 ± 0.44%, and CDR% 93.10 ± 1.2% over 12 h. FTIR, DSC, and XRD confirmed drug amorphization and drug-excipient compatibility. The optimized PoT-PNMs were loaded into freeze-thaw-crosslinked PVA/pHEMA hydrogel contact lenses via soak-loading. The optimized PoT-PNMs -loaded contact lens (NMCL12) showed % transmittance 96.11 ± 0.22%, swelling index 96.48 ± 0.24%, drug content 90.60 ± 0.44%, in-vitro CDR% 96.50 ± 0.30% over 12 h, and mechanical strength 142 ± 6 folds. This system is an effective, scalable method of topical immunomodulatory treatment of inflammatory dry eye disease.

articles.title: Design, Characterization and In Vivo Evaluation of Rifaximin-Loaded Chitosan Nanoparticles for Potential Colonic Drug Delivery in Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop rifaximin (RFX) loaded chitosan (CS)-tripolyphosphate (TPP) nanoparticles for potential colonic delivery as a drug delivery system for the management of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). Nanoparticles were prepared using the ionotropic gelation method and optimized by varying stirring speed, TPP concentration, and polymer-to-drug ratio. The optimized formulation (F41) exhibited a particle size of 262.4 ± 24.3 nm, a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.389 ± 0.033, a zeta potential of + 9.91 ± 0.94 mV, and an encapsulation efficiency (EE%) of 94.75 ± 0.04%. In vitro release studies demonstrated nearly complete drug release within 36 h, which was faster compared to other formulations (52-64 h). Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) confirmed spherical morphology, while differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) analyses indicated successful drug encapsulation without chemical interaction. In vivo evaluation using a chronic restraint stress (CRS) induced IBS model showed that F41 significantly improved physiological parameters, including reduced fecal water content (20.655 ± 23.494%), increased body weight gain (22.716 ± 3.903%), and a decreased disease activity index (p < 0.05). These findings indicate that, the optimized nanoparticle system demonstrated favorable physicochemical properties, sustained drug release, and improved therapeutic outcomes. Owing to the cationic nature of CS, the system may also provide enhanced interaction with colonic mucus, potentially contributing to prolonged local residence. These findings suggest that the developed formulation represents promising approach for potential colonic delivery of RFX in IBS management; however, further studies are required to directly evaluate its mucoadhesive properties and underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: Colorimetric Microplate Assay Coupled with Nonlinear Mixed-Effects Modeling for High-Throughput Evaluation of Ophthalmic Preservatives.
articles.abstract: Conventional preservative efficacy tests for ophthalmic formulations rely on discrete colony counts and therefore provide limited insight into the dynamic processes of microbial inactivation and recovery. Such endpoint-based evaluations can obscure formulation-dependent differences in antimicrobial performance and hinder rational optimization of preservative systems. In this study, we developed a quantitative framework that integrates a high-throughput WST-8-based colorimetric microplate assay with nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) modeling to characterize bacterial killing and regrowth dynamics in borate-buffered systems. Escherichia coli responses were analyzed across 43 formulations using L27 orthogonal and Box-Behnken experimental designs. Bacterial inactivation was described by first-order kinetics, while post-exposure regrowth was modeled using a damage-dependent suppression term. The resulting hierarchical NLME model adequately described bacterial growth trajectories across all formulations, as confirmed by goodness-of-fit diagnostics, visual predictive checks, and bootstrap analyses. Multivariate covariate analysis suggested that borax and pH-related physicochemical conditions contributed to variability in bacterial inactivation rate constants, indicating that antimicrobial activity in borate systems is influenced by buffer composition and the associated physicochemical environment rather than by total borate concentration alone. By coupling structured experimental design with hierarchical population modeling, the proposed framework enables dynamic and mechanism-informed evaluation of preservative efficacy. This approach extends conventional endpoint-based testing and provides a quantitative platform for data-driven optimization and risk assessment of ophthalmic formulations.

articles.title: Assessment of the Mucoadhesion and Mucopermeation of Emulsifying Systems Containing Copaiba Oil on the Intestinal Mucosa.
articles.abstract: Mucopenetrating systems are drug delivery platforms designed to overcome the intestinal mucus barrier, facilitating access to epithelium and enhancing the bioavailability of lipophilic compounds. Copaiba oil (CO) is a compound displaying broad therapeutic potential but low aqueous solubility, which limits its bioavailability. This study aimed to assess how two CO-loaded delivery systems, an emulsion (EM) and a self-emulsifying system (SE), interact with the intestinal mucus layer and how effectively they permeate it. Thus, interactions with mucin and porcine intestinal mucosa were evaluated via oscillatory rheometry, by determining rheological synergism, and the in vitro and ex vivo mucoadhesion assays. The retention of the emulsion systems on the intestinal mucosa was also assessed, along with mucopermeation, using Transwell inserts coated with porcine intestinal mucus and mucin solution. Rheological analysis demonstrated a significant interaction between SE and mucin, evidenced by positive rheological synergism, whereas EM showed limited interaction. In mucoadhesion studies, EM behavior was primarily associated with its higher consistency, while SE exhibited more specific interactions with mucin. Ex vivo retention studies demonstrated greater retention of EM on the intestinal mucosa. In contrast, SE showed superior permeation through the mucus layer in mucopermeation assays, a behavior attributed to the presence of PEG 400. Overall, SE exhibited a more favorable balance between mucoadhesion and mucus penetration than EM. The SE demonstrated enhanced mucopermeation while maintaining adequate interaction with intestinal mucus, suggesting its potential as a promising oral delivery platform for improving the intestinal transport and bioavailability of copaiba oil.

articles.title: Integration of In Silico Degradation Prediction, Mechanistic Stress Testing, and Accelerated Stability Modeling for Olaparib Drug Substance and Prototype Formulation.
articles.abstract: A stability-assessment framework integrating Zeneth in silico degradation prediction, AIBN-mediated radical autoxidation, and ASAPprime® accelerated kinetic modeling was developed for olaparib drug substance and a prototype immediate-release tablet. Zeneth predicted benzylic oxidation as the dominant degradation pathway (pathway score 912). Under AIBN stress, Impurity 6 formed at 2.15%, with radical-initiator dependence confirmed by an AIBN-free control (< 0.1% total impurity); aqueous hydrogen peroxide (1.0%) provided degradant mass for LC-MS/MS characterization. Impurity 6 was confirmed as the benzylic ketone (C₂₄H₂₁FN₄O₄) against an authenticated reference standard (Schymanski Level 1; mass error + 0.7 ppm); the reprocessed HRMS/MS fragmentation ladder was fully reconciled with this assignment, and Impurity 6 was chromatographically resolved from its isomeric Impurity 4 (relative retention times 1.45 versus 1.02). Isoconversion ASAPprime® studies (drug substance: 50-80 °C/11-75% RH; formulation: 40-70°C/11-75% RH) were validated against 12-month real-time data. The drug substance followed first-order kinetics (Ea = 91.2 ± 6.7 kJ·mol⁻1) with negligible humidity sensitivity (B = 0.004 ± 0.003; p > 0.05), yielding a model-derived 95% confidence shelf-life estimate of 3.4 years (MAPD = 5.3%; Q2 = 0.96). The formulation showed accelerated kinetics (Ea = 85.4 ± 5.9 kJ·mol⁻1; B = 0.014 ± 0.005; p < 0.05) and a shelf-life estimate of 2.6 years (MAPD = 5.2%; Q2 = 0.93). These projections require confirmation by longer-term real-time data. The workflow provides a development stage stability risk assessment tool; Impurity 6 was structurally confirmed at Level 1 against an authenticated reference standard, and the formulation was single batch and unoptimized.

articles.title: Overcoming Biopharmaceutical Challenges in the Development of Amorphous Nanosuspension: A Case Study of Atazanavir.
articles.abstract: Amorphous nanosuspensions can generate supersaturated drug concentrations far above crystalline solubility, but their performance depends on stabilizing both the metastable amorphous phase and the high interfacial energy of nanosized particles against recrystallization and Ostwald ripening. ATZ was selected as a model weakly basic drug because its poor dissolution and rapid desupersaturation at intestinal pH provide a rational formulation space for probing the biopharmaceutical relevance of amorphous nanosuspensions. The present study addressed these limitations through the development of ATZ amorphous nanosuspension using acid-base neutralization method. Polymer-surfactant screening was performed through desupersaturation assay and drug-rich droplet size analysis which identified HPMCAS-MG and Soluplus as optimal precipitation inhibitors. Box-Behnken design optimization yielded nanosuspension with a mean particle size of 146.7 ± 5.56 nm and polydispersity index of 0.261 ± 0.05, and a zeta potential of - 4.54 ± 0.78 mV. Solid-state and spectroscopic analyses confirmed successful amorphization of ATZ and the presence of hydrogen-bonding and hydrophobic interactions in ATZ-ANS. Further, non-sink in vitro dissolution testing revealed that ATZ-ANS effectively sustained supersaturation with limited precipitation. The formulation retained its nanoscale characteristics and did not show evidence of recrystallization during six months of accelerated stability testing at 40 °C/75% relative humidity (RH). The in vivo pharmacokinetic evaluation in Sprague Dawley rats demonstrated that ATZ-ANS achieved 16.59-fold higher Cmax (ng/mL) and 6.31-fold higher AUC0-t (ng-h/mL) than crystalline ATZ, and a 2.08-fold and 3.22-fold increase over the marketed formulation (Reyataz®), respectively. Our findings highlighted amorphous nanosuspension as a pragmatic approach for difficult to deliver drugs.
